articles.title: "She wanted to be cherished as an equal": Gisele Bündchen’s shocking relationship rule for Tom Brady revealed years later
articles.summary: Gisele Bündchen reportedly knew exactly what she wanted from her marriage to Tom Brady long before they exchanged vows.
articles.body: Gisele Bündchen reportedly knew exactly what she wanted from her marriage to Tom Brady long before they exchanged vows. According to Lars Anderson’s new biography, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, the supermodel made equality a central part of their relationship. She wanted the pair to build a life as a team while keeping their own identities. Her reported stance offers a revealing look at how Bündchen viewed marriage before their 2009 wedding.Gisele Bündchen wanted an equal partnership with Tom BradyThe conversation reportedly happened before Brady and Bündchen married, when the model shared her vision of what their partnership should look like. Anderson describes Bündchen as a “free spirit” who wanted a relationship built on mutual strength rather than dependence.According to the book, she wanted both partners to contribute while remaining independent people. Anderson writes: “She wanted an interdependent relationship in which the husband and wife were a team,” he wrote. “She stressed the two of them needed to work and rely on each other, but as two whole people with distinct identities. She made it clear she would not accept a codependent relationship built on an imbalance of power, where one partner takes and the other gives.”That distinction was important to Bündchen. She reportedly wanted Brady to be someone who could challenge and inspire her, while also allowing her to do the same for him.Tom Brady agreed with Gisele Bündchen’s relationship visionBündchen reportedly wanted more than a famous husband or successful partner. Anderson says she wanted someone who would grow alongside her, listen to her and take an interest in the different parts of her life.“In every respect, she wanted to be cherished as an equal,” Anderson wrote, adding that “Brady agreed with everything his fiancée said.”The couple first met on a blind date in December 2006 and began dating soon after. Brady proposed in January 2009, and the pair married the following month in California. They later held another wedding celebration in Costa Rica.Their family grew with the births of son Benjamin in 2009 and daughter Vivian in 2012. Brady and Bündchen ultimately divorced in October 2022 after more than a decade of marriage, while continuing to co-parent their children.Bündchen has since moved into a new chapter of her personal life. She began dating jiu-jitsu instructor Joaquim Valente in 2023, welcomed a child with him in 2025 and reportedly married him later that year.The details from Anderson’s biography add another layer to the former couple’s story, showing that equality and personal independence were reportedly priorities for Bündchen from the beginning.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Hailee Steinfeld appears to throw shade at other NFL QBs while praising Josh Allen
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld had no hesitation when asked to name an NFL quarterback during a playful television game, and her answer quickly turned into a sweet
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld had no hesitation when asked to name an NFL quarterback during a playful television game, and her answer quickly turned into a sweet moment for husband Josh Allen. Appearing on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon while promoting her upcoming Disney animated film Hexed, Steinfeld and Fallon were challenged to give different answers to the same prompts. When “NFL Quarterbacks” appeared, both immediately said “Josh Allen.” Steinfeld then jokingly asked, “Are there any others?” The comment drew laughs and gave fans another glimpse into how naturally the Buffalo Bills star comes up in her world.Hailee Steinfeld picks Josh Allen during Tonight Show gameThe moment came during a game designed to test whether Steinfeld and Fallon could think of different answers. Instead, they landed on the same quarterback.Both said Josh Allen, but Steinfeld’s follow-up made the exchange more memorable. “Are there any others?” she asked, jokingly suggesting that her husband was the only name worth mentioning.Fallon played along and said there weren’t any others, while admitting he had not expected Steinfeld to give Allen’s name. The exchange was lighthearted, but it also reflected how closely the couple’s lives now intersect with the NFL spotlight.Steinfeld and Allen married in May 2025 in Santa Barbara after dating for several years. The couple welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in April 2026.Josh Allen’s NFL success gives Hailee Steinfeld plenty to celebrateSteinfeld’s answer also came as Allen and the Bills enjoyed a strong opening to the 2026 season. Buffalo entered the campaign with a 3-0 record, giving the quarterback another reason to dominate football conversations around the couple.Allen’s recent form has added weight to his status as one of the NFL’s leading quarterbacks. Through Buffalo’s first three games, he completed 56 of 86 passes for 786 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions.He also entered the season as the reigning 2024 AP NFL MVP. Allen received 383 voting points and 27 first-place votes, edging Lamar Jackson, who finished with 362 points and 23 first-place votes.Fallon later asked Steinfeld about Buffalo’s unbeaten start and whether she had become superstitious about the team’s success. The actress admitted that she was.“We’re a little ‘stitious, yeah,” said Steinfeld. “How can you not be?”For Steinfeld, cheering for Allen is hardly a new role. articles.title: “We are proud to continue to support”: How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $25,000 foundation move backed college scholarships for Navy SEAL children
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have used their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation to support children in different ways. On Nov.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have used their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation to support children in different ways. On Nov. 11, 2022, the foundation turned its attention to families connected to the U.S. Navy SEALs. It gave the SEAL Legacy Foundation a $25,000 grant to support college scholarships for children of SEALs who made the ultimate sacrifice.The donation went beyond a single scholarship. It supported the Honored SEAL Legacy Scholarship Program, which helps children of fallen Navy SEALs cover college costs. The program honors more than 100 SEALs who have died since 9/11.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes foundation backed a $25,000 scholarship fund for Navy SEAL childrenThe 15 and the Mahomies Foundation announced the $25,000 grant on Veterans Day, Nov. 11, 2022. The money went to the SEAL Legacy Foundation for its Honored SEAL Legacy Scholarship Program, which awards annual college scholarships for academic and related costs to children of U.S. Navy SEALs.The program carries the names of SEALs who lost their lives since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. According to the SEAL Legacy Foundation, each scholarship now carries a $5,000 award and can support tuition, vocational programs, and associate or bachelor’s degree programs.For Patrick, the project also carried a message about remembering the families left behind.“We are proud to continue to support the children of U.S. Navy SEALs through the Honored SEAL Legacy Foundation Scholarship Program,” Mahomes said in the foundation’s Veterans Day announcement on Nov. 11, 2022. “Honoring the work and sacrifice of the SEALs, and providing resources for their families is a core focus of the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.”That focus fits the foundation’s wider work with children and young people. Founded by Mahomes in 2019, 15 and the Mahomies supports programs tied to health, wellness, education and communities that need resources. Its charitable partners also include organizations such as the SEAL Legacy Foundation, Make-A-Wish, Special Olympics Missouri and Boys & Girls Clubs.The scholarship program has supported families of more than 100 fallen SEALsThe 2022 grant was not the foundation’s first connection with the SEAL Legacy Foundation.On May 25, 2020, 15 and the Mahomies announced funding for 15 scholarships through the same Honored SEAL Legacy Scholarship Program. At the time, the foundation said the scholarships would support families of more than 100 Navy SEALs who had died since 9/11.Mahomes also spoke about the foundation’s commitment in that May 25, 2020 announcement, saying, “no one will be left behind.” He made the comment while announcing the 15 scholarships for children of U.S. Navy SEALs through the SEAL Legacy Foundation.The program continues to serve SEAL families. The SEAL Legacy Foundation says its scholarship supports children of active-duty, retired, separated or reserve Navy SEALs. Each $5,000 award can help with tuition and other education costs.For Mahomes and the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, the $25,000 grant showed another side of their charitable work. Instead of focusing on football or athletic programs, the foundation helped families connected to military service and put education at the center of its support.That makes the 2022 Veterans Day contribution a notable part of the Mahomes foundation’s work, especially because the scholarship program continues to honor the children and families of SEALs who never came home.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tyreek Hill's wife testifies about alleged assault, verbal abuse at trial ahead of his potential NFL return
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill is gearing up to sign with an NFL team after a serious knee injury knocked him out early last season.
articles.body:
Content Warning: This story contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

Tyreek Hill's wife detailed the verbal abuse and assaults she suffered throughout their relationship during testimony in the first day of a civil assault-and-battery trial in Florida on Tuesday.

The testimony came just one day after Hill's agent told ESPN that the former star wide receiver could sign with a team in the coming days, potentially even a reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs.

Lakeeta Vaccaro testified during the trial Tuesday, which is part of the couple's divorce proceedings, according to ESPN's Michael Rothstein . Vaccaro, who is the sister of former New Orleans Saints and Tennessee Titans safety Kenny Vaccaro, said that the alleged abuse started in January 2024 when the two were arguing over a post-nuptial agreement Hill was pressuring her to sign. She didn't sign, and said she disagreed with stipulations in the document. Hill then threatened divorce, tried to take her wedding ring off, grabbed a necklace off of her neck, put his hands around her neck, grabbed and twisted her breasts and wrestled her to the bed, she testified. The incident, she said, "terrified" her.

Several other instances of alleged abuse were brought up during the court proceedings on Tuesday. Once, in July 2024, Vaccaro said that Hill attacked her while she was pregnant and tried to punch her in the stomach, which she blocked. In January 2024, while they were on a trip to Orlando, she said that Hill told her that he was going to cheat on her and wanted a divorce. When he came back to their hotel room the next morning, she said he threw her clothes out of a suitcase, broke her computer, took her wedding ring off and twisted one of her breasts. Police were called, but charges were not filed.

Later that month, after an argument about the post-nuptial agreement, Vaccaro said that Hill threw her luggage out of the house, and then Hill physically threw her out. She said that he "ended up throwing or shoving" an unlit cigar butt in her mouth. Police were called then, too.

Vaccaro said that Hill kicked her out of their car while they were driving home from an event in May 2024, and that he threw her shoe out of the car. In November 2024, Vaccaro said that Hill yelled at her and spit in her face after she didn't have a pregame outfit ready for him. She went into labor the next day with their child.

In April 2025, Vaccaro said that Hill punched her computer, threw it to the ground and cursed at her. The argument ended up spilling over into their daughter's room while she was asleep.

"I've been in this cycle with him for so long, being pregnant and realizing, what am I going to do? How am I going to get myself out of this," Vaccaro testified Tuesday, via ESPN. "[The abuse] got worse and worse and worse. And it got to a point where, now I'm a new mom. I have to think of her. I have to think about what I'm putting myself through."

Hill, 31, is working his way back from a serious knee injury that he suffered last season with the Miami Dolphins. His leg was left pointing in the wrong direction, and he was diagnosed with a dislocated kneecap and multiple torn ligaments. The Dolphins released him in February, and he's been a free agent recovering ever since.

Hill previously played six seasons with the Chiefs, and helped them win Super Bowl LIV. The team lost Rashee Rice (hamstring injury) and Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) in the team's win over the Raiders on Sunday .

It's unclear if Hill will face discipline for his alleged abuse from the league if he signs with the Chiefs or elsewhere. The allegations, NFL spokesperson Brian McCarthy told ESPN, remain "under review of the personal conduct policy."

articles.title: Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen faced an unexpected $1,000,000 lawsuit weeks after their wedding over a shocking Costa Rica incident
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen had only been married for weeks when their Costa Rica wedding celebrations turned into a legal fight. In Sept.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen had only been married for weeks when their Costa Rica wedding celebrations turned into a legal fight. In Sept. 2009, two photographers and Agence France-Presse sued the former couple for at least $1 million. They accused security guards linked to the couple of confronting them and firing at their car after they took pictures near the property.The case drew attention because it involved Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, their wedding celebrations and an alleged shooting. But the lawsuit never went to trial in New York. On May 26, 2010, Judge Judith Gische dismissed the case, saying New York did not have jurisdiction over the couple.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced $1 million claims after the Costa Rica incidentThe dispute began during an April 2009 celebration at Gisele Bündchen’s holiday home in Costa Rica. Photographer Yuri Cortez, who worked for Agence France-Presse, and Rolando Aviles of Costa Rican newspaper Al Dia went to cover the couple.The photographers claimed that security guards approached them and demanded their cameras and memory cards. According to their lawsuit, they refused and headed back to their vehicle. They then alleged that security guards fired at the car, damaging its rear windshield.Cortez, Aviles and Agence France-Presse sought at least $1 million in damages when they filed the lawsuit in September 2009. Their complaint also accused Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen of responsibility for the actions of the security team.Brady strongly denied the shooting allegation.In a 2009 interview with Sports Illustrated, while discussing the Costa Rica incident, Brady called the photographers' claims “absolute total b.s.” He also said, “Our security guys didn't even have guns. There were no shots fired.”That gave the case two sharply different accounts. The photographers described a frightening confrontation, while Brady denied that anyone fired a weapon.The legal fight then moved to the question of where the case belonged. The photographers filed in New York, but Judge Judith Gische dismissed the case on May 26, 2010. She said Brady and Bündchen lived in Massachusetts and that the alleged incident happened in Costa Rica.Gische also dismissed the claims against Gisele Bündchen, finding no evidence that she had been involved in hiring or directing the security guards. The ruling did not determine whether the photographers' allegations were true. It only meant the New York court would not hear the case.The Costa Rican legal proceedings involving the security guards continued separately.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen later faced FTX investor lawsuitMore than a decade later, Brady and Bündchen found themselves connected to another high-profile lawsuit, this time over cryptocurrency exchange FTX.After FTX collapsed in Nov. 2022, investors sued several celebrities who promoted the company, including Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen. The plaintiffs argued that celebrity endorsements helped attract customers and alleged violations tied to FTX's business and securities offerings.The case later narrowed. In May 2025, a federal judge dismissed many claims against the celebrity defendants but allowed some claims under Florida and Oklahoma law to continue, according to Reuters.The FTX case differs sharply from the 2009 wedding lawsuit. articles.title: Jermaine Eluemunor: British New York Giants star reveals rise from rock bottom to NFL success story two decades after discovering football in London
articles.summary: Britain's Jermaine Eluemunor opens up on his battle with mental health and inspiring the next generation with his journey to NFL stardom; This story covers themes of mental health, which some may find distressing. If you are affected by this story, please visit sky.com/viewersupport
articles.body:
The Giants offensive tackle dresses up, hosts pretend tea parties and plays the role of punching bag as a proud girl-dad to his young daughters of a week day, and manhandles the greatest athletes on the planet of a weekend. He enjoys the serenity of fishing and escapism of anime off the field, and flourishes in the art of violence on it.

Eluemunor has bridged a transatlantic chasm, swatted away early rejection and overcome 'rock bottom' amid the fiercest of challenges to his mental health to emerge as one of Britain's most gifted footballing exports and, so too, one of the NFL's premier players in his position.

Life wasn't always going to be this way. He now hopes his story can prescribe immunity to the notion of impossible.

"I grew up in Chalk Farm, North West London, right next to Camden Town," Eluemunor tells Sky Sports. "I grew up in a flat on Ferdinand Street, quite small actually, I was just thinking about how small those places were. I went back to see it and I don't even think I fit through the front door now."

It was around this time in 2007 when Eluemunor first discovered football, a session of channel-flicking on TV seeing him stumble across the first-ever NFL regular-season game to be played in London as the Giants faced the Miami Dolphins at Wembley Stadium. Almost two decades on, he is starting for the team where it all began, for whom his impact was rewarded with a $39m contract extension this past offseason and a role as captain this past weekend.

"It was just spur of the moment luck, honestly," he says. "I think that God intended for me to find that game because he knew that was part of my purpose in life to play this game at the highest level and try to achieve what I'm attempting to achieve."

Eluemunor, now 31, moved to New Jersey with his father at the age of 14 in search of greater opportunities, before first playing American football at Morris Knolls High School. His dwarfing stature made an immediate impression, while also prompting some early book-cover-judgement from one coach who made the assumption of a ready-made monster.

"I had never touched a weight in my entire life," he says. "I remember them putting 225 up on the bar and I lifted it up and it fell right on my chest because I wasn't strong at all. Now I can bench over 500 pounds. It was a crazy first day for me, and then just walking around, I'm the English kid."

Despite spending half of his life stateside, he will seemingly forever remain the 'British guy' of NFL locker rooms.

"People still make fun of me for being British every single day, that's never going to go away," he jokes. "I'm literally made fun of for being English every single day, people do English accents every single day."

Still, Eluemunor has never been one to shirk his roots, and this year returned to the UK to stage a four-day camp series that would reach 385 kids. The family of one child notably drove more than two hours each way to attend one of the sessions.

"It's about showing kids that it doesn't matter where you live, where you're from, the colour of your skin, tall, short, big, small, it doesn't matter who you are, you can achieve whatever you want in life," he explained. "I try to be a figure that they can look to as inspiration because I wasn't anything growing up.

"I had dreams, but I didn't know if they were possible to achieve. I want to show these kids that you may not be where you want to be right now, but if you keep working, there's nothing stopping you from achieving what you want to achieve."

His tale is one of patience and persistence. Eluemunor, despite the hundreds of emails he sent to schools across the country, was not initially recruited by any college programs out of high school and as a result joined Lackawanna College. Such was his impact on the football field he was eventually recruited by 35 colleges and spent three years with Texas A&M before being selected by the Baltimore Ravens in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. The transition, as it had been upon arriving in the US, would prove anything but an easy weight to shift.

He made just three starts in his first two seasons with the Ravens, remembering vividly of the fans that had claimed he 'sucked' while suggesting he did not belong in the NFL. Eluemunor was ultimately traded to the New England Patriots in August 2019, prompting the most difficult and yet most defining chapter of his career.

"It shaped me completely," he says. "I was the lowest of the lowest in New England, it was pretty tough, really tough.

"I learned a lot about myself. I learned a lot about what it took to really belong in this league. But then also I learned that mentally, I'm a lot stronger than I think I am. If I can get through that, I can get through anything."

Eluemunor was limited to 29 snaps on offense in his first campaign in New England, his progress hindered by an ankle injury in Week Six before a Patriots teammate fell on his leg upon his return to practice, leaving him in tears amid another setback to his career.

He admits he became guilty of buying into criticism he read on social media and in turn speaking negatively about himself, at one stage crying to Patriots trainer Daryl Nelson amid his troubled efforts to transition to a new role at left tackle.

"Everyone has a goal and a dream, and when you feel that thing slip away and you feel there's nothing you can do to control that, you kind of just go into a spiral. And before you know, you can hit rock bottom," he explains.

"In order to get out of rock bottom, it takes certain people to pull you from that, you can't do it alone. You need people to help you along the way. I had great people in my life that truly helped pull me out from rock bottom and put me on the path that I needed to be on.

"I'm a very lucky person because not a lot of people can get all the way to rock bottom and be able to pull themselves out and make something of themselves. I'm a lucky person, but I also work really, really hard, I worked really hard to get away from that mentally and I worked really hard to get where I'm at now."

At his lowest, he would have to field questions as to whether he ever thought about taking his own life, previously insisting he never quite strayed as far as that idea, largely thanks to a devoted support network led by his wife Christina.

"I think that nowadays mental health is such a huge thing, I think the more people are willing to be open about it, the better things will be," he explains.

"A lot of the times we think that we have to be these strong, tough, imposing figures, especially being an offensive lineman in the NFL, people start to think of you as superhero-esque and they don't think that you're a normal person.

"But to be able to share the way you feel and what you're going through and show just how normal you really are, I think that goes a long way in shedding light on subjects that are a little bit more sensitive, especially when it comes to mental health.

"If you can learn how to control the narrative and just work hard and really be vulnerable and open with people, then you'll see that people are way more accepting than you think and believe. Then you find a great group or team like I've been lucky enough to find with the Giants, then people just fall in love with you and the person you are and you don't have to be someone you're not and you're able to just be yourself."

Eluemunor became a free agent following the 2020 season before being cut by both the Miami Dolphins and Jacksonville Jaguars during preseason. He then signed with the Las Vegas Raiders and made three starts at right guard before being benched for the remainder of the season.

He was handed a one-year $1.3m deal to stay with the team in 2022, paving the way for his most productive year yet as Eluemunor started all 17 games to earn a $3m extension. Criticism of his work ethic and attitude from interim coach Rich Bisaccia had ignited a dogged reply; the physical attributes to dominate and the potential to cement a starting spot in the NFL had always been there to be unlocked, and everybody knew it. Coaches were desperate to see Eluemunor fulfil as much, and put on a smile while doing so.

Still, for all his progress, Eluemunor remained conscious to his struggles in New England and the lingering threat of slipping back into the same headspace. He was put in contact with mental health coach Brian Cain, who later made Eluemunor a "mental movie" that he could watch before playing, depicting images of his loved ones along with some of his best moments on the field.

"I watch it before every game because it kind of puts perspective into place and shows me why I do what I do and what I need to do to go out there and be successful. he's been a huge person for me," he says.

"I have my baby girls and I do this for my wife, that's my reason, that's my why. I want them to go back and look at my career and be like, you know, our dad did this for us and he was one of the best players, if not the best player in his position when we were kids.

"I want them to be like, he did everything, accomplished everything he wanted to accomplish, so there's no reason why we can't accomplish what we want to accomplish."

It is the same message he continues to relay to the children he meets during camps such as the one this past summer in the UK.

"Mental health is such a sensitive subject, especially with the younger generation, that you have to be able to be vulnerable and show them who you truly are," he continues. "When I put the face mask on, I'm still the same person. And I want to show them that, just because I'm a professional athlete and make all this money, it doesn't mean I'm different from any of you.

"I try to show them every single day that we're not too far apart and we're not any different than each other. It's the person you are deep within you who makes you who you are."

The Jermaine Eluemunor of today will tell you he is the best right tackle in the NFL. Of that much he holds zero doubts.

He will publicly welcome the prospect of being left one-on-one on an island against the TJ Watts of the world, eager to test himself against the best and equally convinced that he will come out on top. As of Week Four this season, no offensive tackle has been left on an 'island' at a higher rate than Eluemunor's 71.4 per cent, according to Pro Football Focus; what's more, he has won those battles 93.7 per cent of the time.

"I've grown a lot mentally," he says. "I can look back at that kid in New England and say that I'm a million times the player I was mentally and physically.

"You have to go through things like that in order to get to where you want to get to and become the person you want to become. I believe that was a trial that I put in my life and to see if I was going to make it through to truly become who I want to become.

"I've always been driven to be the best. I just didn't do the work that was required to be the best."

Eluemunor signed a two-year deal with the Giants back in March 2024 and has since established himself as an instrumental piece to his team's offensive line. It has taken countless trials and obstacles to get here, but there is now a sense of long-awaited stability and momentum capable of inciting the best version of the man from Chalk Farm, London.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs, prior to me getting to New York there was a lot more downs than ups. I've just had to work really, really hard to get to where I'm at," he said.

"I've just kept working my butt off trying to be great. I want to be as great as possible. I want to be the greatest. I want to be the best in my position."

It's way too early to focus on tiebreakers but the Colts have legitimate playoff hopes (for now).

articles.title: Week 5 NFL power rankings: Where Indianapolis Colts rank among 2-2 teams
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts improve their record, but that doesn't necessarily equate to a boost in the NFL power rankings.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are one of 11 NFL teams with a 2-2 record, but are "average" squads made the same?

They posted a 17-point win in Week 4 , their largest since Week 8 of last season. That's impressive, right?

The NFL power rankings aren't convinced, placing the Colts low among .500 teams.

NFL power rankings: Indianapolis Colts rank poorly among 2-2 teams

The Athletic : 19th, unchanged from last week, 8th among 2-2 teams

"The Colts went to London and didn't have to do much to beat up on the undermanned Washington Commanders . But there's rising concern about Daniel Jones, who completed 19-of-34 passes for just 143 yards with no touchdowns and an interception in his return from an Achilles injury."

Aaron Leming, SB Nation : 23rd, last among 2-2 teams

"Following an 0-2 start, the Colts have fought their way back to .500. While that might look good on paper, the quality of those two wins is questionable at best. This team has far too much money tied up in key positions at quarterback and on defense, and it hasn't gotten the desired return thus far. That might be the key to getting this season back on track and back into the playoffs."

Frank Schwab, Yahoo : 22nd, down 3, 10th among 2-2 teams

"Injuries at receiver have been an issue. Missing Alec Pierce changes how defenses approach the Colts, without the threat of big plays downfield. Still, Daniel Jones looks much worse than he did last season, and it's fair to wonder if his Achilles tear plays a part in that. He still has the support of Colts coach Shane Steichen, who said Jones is doing a good job."

Vinnie Iyer, Sporting News : 23rd, up 1, last among 2-2 teams

"The Colts needed some schedule breaks after facing the Ravens and Chiefs to open the season. They got them from the Texans and Commanders with Jonathan Taylor and the defense making it easier on Daniel Jones. Getting the Steelers and Titans next can keep Indy hot."

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

Pete Prisco, CBS Sports : 22nd, down 2, 10th among 2-2 teams

"At 2-2, they have righted things after opening 0-2. They wised up in the victory over the Commanders and gave the ball to Jonathan Taylor."

Brent Sobleski, Bleacher Report : 23rd, unchanged, last among 2-2 teams

"Shane Steichen's squad isn't close to where it was before last season's second-half collapse. Quarterback Daniel Jones was a huge part of that early success. He's been part of the problem to start this season despite the two-game winning streak."

Nate Davis, USA TODAY : 23rd, up 1, 10th among 2-2 teams

"Maybe they should pack the Mayflower trucks (ships?) for Europe given they've won three in a row in the Old World, which the NFL seems ready to make its new frontier."

Mike Florio, Pro Football Talk : 22nd, up 2, 10th among 2-2 teams

"Can they win enough games to steal a wild-card berth?"

Conor Orr, Sports Illustrated : 17th, down 2, 6th among 2-2 teams

"I don't really care what happens to this iteration of the Colts, but following the Sauce Gardner trade last year, literally the only sensible follow-up is to continue pouring resources into this team and trading for Colts legacy son Marvin Harrison Jr."

articles.title: NY Giants fans think Odell Beckham Jr. call aged poorly as replacement gets season-ending surgery
articles.summary: The New York Giants released Odell Beckham Jr. after just a few games, hoping Braxton Berrios could replace him.
articles.body:
The New York Giants released Odell Beckham Jr. after just a few games, hoping Braxton Berrios could replace him.

However, Berrios, who was signed to the Giants' practice squad after Beckham was released, is now set to undergo season-ending surgery.

This leaves the Giants light on depth at the WR position, especially after releasing Beckham. And fans are concerned the franchise may have made a mistake.

New York Giants fans believe team cut Odell Beckham Jr. 'for nothing' after Braxton Berrios injury

Against the Arizona Cardinals, New York Giants WR Braxton Berrios suffered a foot injury that forced him out of the game early on.

The injury appears to be worse than initially thought, as Berrios has undergone season-ending foot surgery to address the issue.

Understandably, Giants fans and NFL fans as a whole pointed out how much this decision looks even worse in the aftermath of the franchise releasing Odell Beckham Jr.

One fan simply wrote, "Giants should've treated my boy right," while another fan added, "So they cut Odell for nothing."

A third fan pointed to the timeline of the situation to highlight the comedy of errors, noting, "They cut OBJ, signed Berrios, and now Berrios is done for the season. Great work, guys."

"Giants have a plague with injuries this season that I've never seen before. Oh my days," wrote a fourth fan, pointing to the other high-profile injuries to players like Jaxson Dart along with Berrios.

A fifth fan suggested the Giants might reach out to Beckham Jr., noting, "That call to OBJ gonna be so awkward."

"They let go of OBJ for this guy, and he gets hurt on the first start? WTH is going on in the NFL? I know OBJ is thinking what I'm thinking," joked a sixth fan, trying to suggest Beckham Jr. was happy with this situation.

And lastly, one fan shut down any notion of Beckham Jr. being brought back, saying, "Peeps saying sign OBJ. Dude is old and washed. You don't win games by aura farming."

Even with this injury to Berrios, it is highly unlikely that the Giants will bring back Odell Beckham Jr., given that the release seemed to cause a permanent rift in their relationship.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 5
articles.summary: We're only a month into the 2026 season, but we've already seen some significant activity on the trade market due to injuries and pressing contract situations.
articles.body:
We're only a month into the 2026 season, but we've already seen some significant activity on the trade market due to injuries and pressing contract situations.

Last week, the New York Giants acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings, a response to losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury. The Pittsburgh Steelers then traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys amid a prolonged contract dispute.

According to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , the decision followed another report of back pain from the cornerback, one day after the team listed him as a full participant in practice.

While Porter may be the last contract hold-in to be dealt this season, he won't be the last player traded. Injuries continue to mount, and teams are beginning to spiral out of the playoff picture—all five 0-3 teams fell to 0-4 this past week.

Here is an updated look at our top 10 trade candidates, ranked by past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, projected availability, and any relevant recent rumors.

We'll dive into players that teams should be targeting, project trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, and identify a few logical suitors.

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

To be clear, Mac Jones remains the best quarterback for teams in need of an immediate starter to target.

The 28-year-old went 5-3 with a 97.4 passer rating as the San Francisco 49ers' starter in 2025, and he could steer another playoff-caliber team to the postseason in 2026 if needed.

However, the 49ers aren't going to let Jones go for cheap. San Francisco wanted a second-round pick for him in the spring, according to The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt , and the more the Niners believe a Super Bowl run is possible, the less likely they will be to part with their insurance at quarterback.

Brock Purdy hasn't been sacked yet this season, but the Niners have experienced enough other early injuries to value proven depth behind him.

With quarterbacks like Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels getting closer to a return, there isn't a clear suitor that would pay the hefty price to pry Jones out of San Francisco right now. That could change before November 10, though, and we could see teams that lack a QB plan beyond 2026 enter the mix as well.

Potential Suitors: Arizona Cardinals, New York Jets

9. Jadeveon Clowney, Edge, Houston Texans

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick

Pass-rushers are always valued around the trade deadline, which is why several reside on our top-10 list.

First up is Jadeveon Clowney, who returned late in the offseason to the team that drafted him. The first overall pick in the 2014 draft signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Houston Texans and believed he'd be joining a title contender. However, the Texans have looked like anything but during their 0-4 start to the season.

The Texans could still get back in the playoff mix, but they could be prompted to send Clowney to a contender for a strong return—which they should be able to get.

Houston could also save $3.3 million in cap space by moving the 33-year-old.

Clowney had 8.5 sacks and 22 quarterback pressures with the Dallas Cowboys last season. He returned from a two-game absence due to a bone bruise in his knee and recorded a half-sack against Dallas in Week 4.

In two games this season, Clowney has recorded 1.5 sacks and four QB pressures. He should interest most teams in need of pass-rushing help this season.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Dallas Cowboys

8. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick

While the demand for a fill-in starter may be dwindling, the market for a backup QB may be heating up.

The Washington Commanders may be close to having Daniels back, but backup Marcus Mariota is now dealing with an MCL injury . While Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated thumb, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking at Easton Stick behind undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels.

An increased backup-QB market could benefit the Pittsburgh Steelers, who were reportedly open to moving Mason Rudolph at the start of the season, according to Jason La Canfora of Casino.org.

Rudolph, who has 20 career starts (including playoffs), is one of the league's better backups. He could also be viewed as expendable, as Pittsburgh has Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar behind Aaron Rodgers.

Potential Suitors: Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Washington Commanders

Buyers or Sellers for NFL's Most Surprising Teams 🏈

7. Marvin Harrison Jr., WR, Arizona Cardinals

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 3rd-Round Pick

The Arizona Cardinals have lost three straight and are looking like a team that may soon begin playing for 2027 and beyond.

Arizona's quarterback of the future probably isn't on the current roster, though the Cardinals have several promising offensive pieces they can eventually put around him. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love all project as long-term building blocks, though 2024 first-round pick Marvin Harrison Jr. may not.

Harrison was widely viewed as a "can't-miss" prospect when the Cardinals drafted him fourth overall. However, he has fallen behind in Arizona's offensive game plan and could probably use a change of scenery .

Unfortunately, it appears that Harrison's trade value is at an all-time low—some teams believe he may not command more than a Day-3 pick, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

The Cardinals probably won't let Harrison go for that low a price, but it feels like a team willing to bet on his upside could snag him before the deadline.

Potential Suitors: Indianapolis Colts, Kansas City Chiefs

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 7th-Round Draft Pick

Like the Texans, the Tennessee Titans are sitting at 0-4 and staring down a lost season. The AFC South rivals face one another in Week 5, giving both a chance to secure their first win. However, Tennessee feels much further away from turning things around than Houston does.

Let's not forget that the Texans rebounded from a 0-3 start last year and still made the postseason. The Titans went 3-14 in each of the past two campaigns.

Tennessee will likely use the rest of 2026 to evaluate quarterback Cam Ward and determine whether it should consider replacing him with a top 2027 prospect. Veteran players who won't contribute toward that goal should be viewed as expendable.

The Titans traded for defensive lineman Solomon Thomas in the offseason, reuniting him with head coach Robert Saleh. While Thomas has appeared in all four games this season, he has played just 25 percent of the defensive snaps.

Thomas, who will be a free agent in 2027, has little long-term value to the Titans. However, he could bolster a contender's defensive line.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Cleveland Browns

5. Walker Little, OT, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick and/or Veteran Defender

The Jacksonville Jaguars moved to 3-1 on Saturday, and they certainly aren't going to sell off pieces the way that the league's winless teams might. However, they have a high-priced backup in Walker Little who could draw significant interest in the wake of more offensive tackle injuries.

The Cardinals, for example, recently placed starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. on injured reserve with a torn bicep . He'll miss the remainder of the 2026 season.

Little was a starter for the Jaguars before losing his job at left tackle to Cole Van Lanen. He has appeared in all four games this season but has played just 24 offensive snaps and 21 snaps on special teams.

With 39 starts on his resume, Little should bring a moderate return on the trade market. Jacksonville would also save $11.4 million in cap space by moving him.

Potential Suitors: Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers

4. Kenneth Gainwell, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Injuries continue to mount at running back across the NFL. Jadarian Price, Tank Bigsby, and Travis Etienne Jr. have all recently landed on injured reserve, and Miami Dolphins starter De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL.

The Buccaneers, who are sitting at 0-4 with an undrafted rookie at quarterback, could cash in on the run of injuries by moving backup Kenneth Gainwell.

Gainwell signed a two-year, $14 million deal in the offseason to back up Bucs starter Bucky Irving. The Buccaneers would save just $2 million in 2026 cap space by trading the 27-year-old, but they could clear his 2027 $7 million cap hit from the books while getting a reasonable return.

While Gainwell did score his first touchdown for Tampa in Week 4, he has still logged a mere 21 touches through four weeks. However, he racked up 187 touches, 1,023 scrimmage yards, and eight touchdowns with the Steelers last season.

At this point in the season, Gainwell would boost the backfield depth of multiple teams.

Potential Suitors: Philadelphia Eagles, Seattle Seahawks

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Dolphins haven't really hidden the fact that they're playing for the future in 2026. They gambled on quarterback Malik Willis in free agency, but they dumped most of their noteworthy veterans during the offseason.

The Dolphins do have some nice young pieces on their roster and just played a very competitive game against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. However, they're still sitting at 0-4 and are highly unlikely to get in the AFC East race at any point this season.

While Miami may not be interested in parting with any more potential long-term building blocks—like 23-year-old edge-defender Chop Robinson—it should be willing to move pass-rusher Josh Uche. The 28-year-old has been a veteran leader early in the season but is only playing on a one-year deal.

Uche recorded his first sack of the season against Minnesota, and he has logged four QB pressures and 17 total tackles through four weeks. He should be very attractive to teams that either lack edge-rushing depth or have lost it to injury during the first month of the season.

Potential Suitors: New York Giants, Philadelphia Eagles

The Cleveland Browns moved to 3-1 with a win over the Steelers in Week 4.

During their latest victory, they got a handful of clutch catches from veteran receiver Jerry Jeudy. According to Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com, the Browns aren't interested in trading the 27-year-old right now.

However, Cabot's report clashes with that of ESPN insider Adam Schefter.

"Jeudy is being squeezed out. He could be had by the trade deadline," Schefter told NFL Sunday Countdown (beginning around the 46-second mark).

Jeudy is being "squeezed out" of the offense by promising rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston , who have quickly emerged as go-to targets. While Jeudy did play a role in Cleveland's latest win, he's caught just five of eight targets for 62 yards on the season.

A 1,200-yard receiver and a Pro Bowler in 2024, Jeudy should interest receiver-needy teams, as should his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million .

Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, Philadelphia Eagles

1. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Los Angeles Chargers made the playoffs in their first two years under head coach Jim Harbaugh, and most viewed them as 2026 playoff contenders. However, the Chargers are now among the league's winless teams and are potentially looking at a lost season.

This isn't the sort of situation Khalil Mack believed he was joining when he re-signed on a one-year, $18 million deal this offseason.

Mack has not been part of the disappointment in Los Angeles, as he's off to a very strong start to the season. He's already logged 14 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, and eight quarterback pressures.

The Chargers won't be eager to move Mack as long as they believe they can rebound. If they believe their season is lost, however, they could save $8 million in cap space by moving him.

They could also expect a strong return for the 35-year-old, who has the potential to push a playoff-caliber defense into championship territory.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: B/R's Week 5 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is a month old, and fantasy managers have already experienced quite a roller-coaster ride.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is a month old, and fantasy managers have already experienced quite a roller-coaster ride.

Big-name players getting hurt? Early-round picks disappointing? Absolutely—especially among the Los Angeles Chargers. Late-round picks breaking out? Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young sits third in fantasy points at his position.

The constantly shifting fantasy landscape is enough to give fantasy managers vertigo, especially if they are already queasy after a poor start.

This column can help settle those lineup worries—at least for one week. It's a guide to Week 5, with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to this week's player rankings, a few notes.

The first is the same as always: The list of the top 125 players overall for Week 5 (a list that can aid in flex decisions) does not contain quarterbacks. If you play in a superflex league and have a viable QB2, he should be in that spot.

The second is a minor drag that will eventually become a major one: The bye weeks have started. The Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs are off, so no Kenneth Walker III, Travis Kelce or Tetairoa McMillan in Week 5.

Finally, I know how frustrating it can be to start a season 1-3 or 0-4. It's tempting to throw up your hands and give up. But staying competitive keeps the league engaging for everyone—and there's still time to try to turn things around.

Even if the playoffs aren't in the cards, you can still play spoiler and make your leaguemates sweat.

Injuries are an unfortunate reality of the NFL—and a recurring challenge for fantasy managers. Every season, players get hurt, and it can feel as though the injury list is longer than ever.

This year, though, those concerns may be justified, especially at quarterback. According to ESPN's Bill Barnwell , eight quarterbacks were unavailable because of injury under his criteria through the first three weeks of the 2026 season—the highest total at that point since 1999.

The injuries kept coming in Week 4. The Washington Commanders may have little choice but to start Jayden Daniels (elbow) this week. After Marcus Mariota sprained his knee last week in London, the team was forced to turn to Athan Kaliakmanis under center. In Baltimore, Lamar Jackson suffered an ankle injury that could sideline him for multiple games .

After a red-hot start to the season that included two games with 35-plus fantasy points, Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills has cooled off. He remains fantasy's No. 1 quarterback , but after 253 yards and one passing score last week against the Patriots, he has failed to hit 20 points in back-to-back games.

Elsewhere, Justin Herbert's nightmare season for the Los Angeles Chargers rolls on. He threw for 189 yards and a touchdown with two interceptions in last week's loss to the Seattle Seahawks, and he has yet to post even a 15-point game this season.

Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals had his best fantasy effort of the season last week against the Jacksonville Jaguars—428 yards, a passing score and a rushing touchdown. However, Burrow also lost wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) to injuries, so there are major questions surrounding the Bengals passing game in Week 5.

Jacoby Brissett, Arizona Cardinals (vs. Detroit Lions)

Brissett threw for just 166 yards a week ago, although he threw multiple touchdown passes for the second straight game. His best game of the season should be coming in Week 5—the Lions are allowing a whopping 304 passing yards per game this season.

Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (at Seattle Seahawks)

Purdy is playing like an MVP candidate this season, and he's the highest-scoring fantasy quarterback in the NFC. But he is coming off his worst statistical outing of the season, and this week he takes on a Seahawks team surrendering less than 145 yards per contest.

Jameis Winston, New York Giants (at Washington Commanders)

Week 4 was Jameis Winston in a nutshell: 250 passing yards, three touchdowns and a pair of interceptions. The Giants draw a great matchup for quarterbacks this week—the Commanders have given up the third-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season.

Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions and Bijan Robinson of the Atlanta Falcons were the first two picks in many fantasy drafts over the summer. A month into the season, neither has disappointed.

Gibbs was held somewhat in check by the Carolina Panthers last week—77 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. But that was his first game this season with fewer than 100 total yards. He has scored a touchdown in all four games and is averaging a gaudy 29 PPR points per game.

Meanwhile, Robinson is rolling in Atlanta's run-heavy offense. Monday night against the New Orleans Saints, he rolled for 145 rushing yards and two scores, his second straight game with at least that many yards on the ground and multiple touchdowns.

The quarterback position isn't the only spot that has been hit by injuries this season, and a big name in the backfield went down in Week 4.

Saquon Barkley of the Philadelphia Eagles pulled his hamstring in a loss to the Los Angeles Rams, and while the injury isn't believed to be serious, he is going to miss time.

Barkley wasn't the only back who got nicked up in Week 4. Toward the end of his 146-yard, two-score outburst against the New York Jets, Kyle Monangai of the Chicago Bears suffered a thumb injury. However, there is optimism that he will be OK for this week's trip to Green Bay.

Fantasy managers of Chase Brown of the Cincinnati Bengals were OK with the results of his Week 4 matchup with the Jaguars—his 19.1 PPR points ranked inside the top-15 at the position. But his bacon was saved by a jaw-dropping 11 catches—the fourth-year veteran had nine carries for 10 yards and is averaging a career-low 3.6 yards per carry this year.

Aaron Jones, Minnesota Vikings (at New Orleans Saints)

The Minnesota offense has struggled mightily in recent weeks, but Jones has done his part—his 128 total yards last week against the Arizona Cardinals marked the second time in three weeks he has hit triple-digits. He has a favorable opportunity to make it three of four this week against the Saints' non-existent run defense.

Will Shipley, Philadelphia Eagles (at Jacksonville Jaguars)

With Barkley dealing with a hamstring issue and Tank Bigsby headed to injured reserve with a groin injury, Shipley could take on a larger role in the Eagles' backfield. However, he faces a difficult matchup this week against Jacksonville's strong run defense.

Woody Marks, Houston Texans (at Tennessee Titans)

On a per-carry basis, Marks has been more effective than David Montgomery this season, although neither back has found much running room this year. That should change in Week 5—the Tennessee Titans are allowing almost 123 yards per game on the ground and giving up 20.6 PPR points per game to running backs.

We'll cover the long list of injured wide receivers in this week's notes. First, though, let's highlight two standout performances at the position last week.

The first came in Houston, where CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys roasted the Texans defense to the tune of 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown. It marked the second time this season that the five-time Pro Bowler has piled up 35 PPR points, and only Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks has scored more points among wide receivers.

Sunday night in Carolina, Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan tried his level best to best Lamb's explosion. The 2025 No. 8 overall pick roasted Detroit's miserable defense for 14 receptions, 192 yards and two touchdowns.

If you started either player, odds are Week 4 turned out OK.

We have already mentioned that both Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) were forced from Cincinnati's loss to the Jaguars, but they weren't the only big names at the position who got hurt last week.

In Buffalo's loss to the New England Patriots, D.J. Moore aggravated his shoulder injury. Things just keep getting worse for Ladd McConkey of the Los Angeles Chargers, who hurt his foot in Sunday's defeat in Seattle.

Rashee Rice of the Kansas City Chiefs pulled his hamstring in the first quarter against the Raiders and did not return, and Mack Hollins of the New England Patriots injured his calf.

Mind you, this was in a week when multiple wideouts like DeVonta Smith of the Philadelphia Eagles (hamstring), Justin Jefferson of the Minnesota Vikings (ankle) and Jalen Coker of the Carolina Panthers (quad) were already sidelined.

That's not even a complete list. Injuries have left fantasy managers with plenty of difficult lineup decisions this week.

Michael Wilson, Arizona Cardinals (vs. Detroit Lions)

Wilson has been hot the past two weeks, with 18 receptions for 184 yards and a touchdown over his last two games. The good times should keep rolling Sunday against the Lions—no team in the NFC is allowing more PPR points to wide receivers this season.

Christian Watson, Green Bay Packers (vs. Chicago Bears)

The Packers have been struggling to move the football this season, but Watson has been solid for fantasy managers—he's fifth in PPR points among wide receivers this year after four games. But he is coming off his worst statistical effort of the year and faces the risk of a second straight disappointing outing in a bottom-five fantasy matchup with the Bears.

Isaac TeSlaa, Detroit Lions (at Arizona Cardinals)

TeSlaa had his best game of the season in last week's loss to the Carolina Panthers, catching four of eight targets for 95 yards. He is averaging almost 21 yards per reception this year, and with the Lions in weekly shootouts he's a sneaky-good start against a Cardinals team that has surrendered the sixth-most PPR points to wideouts in 2026.

There have been two tight ends who have posted double-digit PPR points in all four games. The first is no surprise: Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals.

However, the second is an eyebrow-raiser. It's not Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs, George Kittle of the San Francisco 49ers or Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders.

It's Juwan Johnson of the New Orleans Saints.

After six catches for 59 yards Monday night against the Atlanta Falcons, Johnson is fourth among tight ends in targets (27), sixth at the position in receptions (21), fifth in receiving yards (232), tied for second in touchdowns (3) and third in PPR points.

Not bad for a tight end who was drafted outside the top 15 at the position on average over the summer.

The tight end position hasn't been hit as hard by injuries as wide receiver, but there are a couple of banged-up guys. Dallas Goedert of the Philadelphia Eagles has missed the last two games with an MCL sprain that will likely sideline him again in Week 5, while Terrance Ferguson of the Rams landed on injured reserve with an injured ankle.

Kyle Pitts has been invisible this year. He caught three passes for 47 yards in Monday's win over the Saints, which is more catches and yards than he had in the first three games of the season combined.

The highest-scoring tight end in fantasy in Week 4 was something of a surprise—T.J. Hockenson of the Minnesota Vikings had more PPR points in Week 4 than he did in the first three games combined, catching 13 passes for 119 yards. The week could have been even bigger, but Hockenson passed on a late touchdown so the Vikings could run out the clock.

Mike Gesicki, Cincinnati Bengals (at Miami Dolphins)

Gesicki has quietly been solid this season for the Bengals and fantasy managers alike, finding the end zone in three of four games this season. Now he faces a Miami Dolphins team allowing the fourth-most PPR points to tight ends this season.

Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers (vs. Chicago)

Kraft is coming off a good outing against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, setting a season-high with six catches and finding the end zone for the first time this season. It could be difficult to match those numbers against the Bears, who have surrendered the third-fewest PPR points to tight ends in 2026.

Greg Dulcich, Miami Dolphins (vs. Cincinnati Bengals)

The Miami passing attack has barely been passable this season, but if Dulcich is ever going to have a week, this is it. The Cincinnati Bengals just gave up a big stat line to Brenton Strange of the Jaguars, and Cincy has struggled to defend tight ends for years.

We're combining team defenses and kickers this week to cover your final lineup decisions in one place.

For fantasy managers, success on defense lies in big plays: sacks and takeaways. Given the aggressiveness of Brian Flores' defense with the Minnesota Vikings, it should come as no surprise that they rank at or near the top of the league in both categories. Or that they lead all defenses in fantasy points.

To say Flores likes to get after opposing quarterbacks is an understatement. In an NFL where no other team has a blitz percentage of 50, the Vikings send an extra man more than 72 percent of the time.

Don't look now, but a month into the 2026 season, the Jacksonville Jaguars have one of the NFL's better defenses. Ahead of this week's London tilt with the Philadelphia Eagles, the Jaguars lead the AFC in both run defense and scoring defense. Jacksonville is tied for the NFL's sixth-most sacks, rank second in the league in takeaways and have posted more fantasy points than any AFC defense.

While the Jaguars are rolling, the winless Houston Texans are reeling—and a disappointing defense has played a significant role in Houston's 0-4 start. After leading the league in total defense and pacing the AFC in points allowed a year ago, the Texans have allowed the sixth-most yards and seventh-most points in the NFL in 2026.

The Indianapolis Colts have had a mixed start at 2-2, but placekicker Spencer Shrader has excelled. The 27-year-old leads all kickers in fantasy points and has made all 11 of his field-goal attempts, including all four from 50-plus yards.

Denver Broncos Defense (at Los Angeles Chargers)

Like the Texans, the Broncos have struggled a bit defensively, at least from a fantasy perspective. This week's trip to Los Angeles is a "get right" spot—the Bolts have given up the most fantasy points in the AFC to defenses.

Brandon Aubrey, Dallas Cowboys (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

After a down Week 1, Aubrey has peeled off three straight games with double-digit fantasy points. He has a strong chance to make it four in a row Thursday night against a Buccaneers squad giving up the most fantasy points to kickers this year.

Seattle Seahawks (vs. San Francisco 49ers)

Seattle's "Dark Side" defense has been solid for fantasy managers this season, ranking sixth among fantasy defenses in points. But this week's matchup with the 49ers looks difficult, with Brock Purdy limiting turnovers and avoiding sacks.

Trey Smack, Green Bay Packers (vs. Chicago Bears)

Given the overall struggles of Green Bay's offense this season, it's not surprising that Smack hasn't made much of a fantasy dent. That's not likely to change this week against a Bears team surrendering the third-fewest fantasy points to kickers this season.

Chris Boswell, Pittsburgh Steelers (vs. Indianapolis Colts)

Boswell hasn't been especially productive this year and ranks outside the top 20 at the position in fantasy points this year. But he should have more scoring opportunities this week against a leaky Colts defense.

Dallas Cowboys Defense (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

The supposedly improved Dallas defense in 2026 looks a lot like the Cowboys did a year ago, which is to say bad. But Dallas is hosting a Buccaneers team leading the league in fantasy points allowed to defenses starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback.

Gary Davenport ("The Godfather of IDP") is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow him on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Ranking the Best 10 Bills Players of All Time
articles.summary: Few franchises in professional football boast a history as distinct, emotionally charged, and star-studded as the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Few franchises in professional football boast a history as distinct, emotionally charged, and star-studded as the Buffalo Bills.

Across four definitive eras—the punishing American Football League championship squads of the mid-1960s, the ground-churning 1970s "Electric Company" that powered the league's first 2,000-yard rusher, the revolutionary 1990s no-huddle machine that captured four consecutive AFC crowns, and the modern juggernaut resurrected by Josh Allen—Buffalo's identity has always been forged by transcendent, blue-collar talent.

Ranking the franchise's all-time greatest players requires balancing elite individual peaks against sustained longevity and overall organizational impact. It isn't an easy process. It requires frequent updates as we watch Allen dominate the league year after year in the current era.

Regardless, for now, these 10 icons stand above the rest as the definitive pillars of Buffalo Bills football.

Cornelius Bennett: A member of the 1990s All-Decade Team, he earned five Pro Bowl nods over the course of nine seasons in Buffalo. Bennett was consistently a key ingredient during a wildly successful era in team history, but rarely a superstar.

Darryl Talley: An emotional leader and high-impact warrior, Talley was a tackle machine during a 12-year run with the Bills. That said, he was a Pro Bowler just twice and never a first-team All-Pro. An argument could be made that Bennett and Talley prevent each other from making the top 10. It doesn't help that both were overshadowed by the league's all-time sack leader.

Steve Tasker: Quite possibly the greatest special teams player in league history, Tasker hits an inescapable ceiling because of his snap counts.

Butch Byrd: He remains the franchise's all-time leader in interceptions (40) and pick-sixes (5), while anchoring the defense for two AFL titles. Byrd's peak in Western New York was still relatively compressed. He was a first- or second-team All-Pro four times in a five-season span but was off the roster a year later.

The Snapshot: An extremely durable leader of the offensive line for 11 years who engineered the breakneck tempo of the K-Gun offense during the most successful run for the team in the Super Bowl era.

Claim to Fame: Orchestrating the pre-snap protections and shotgun snaps across 169 starts and four consecutive Super Bowl seasons.

The Body of Work: A three-time Pro Bowler and four-time first- or second-team All-Pro, Hull started 121 consecutive regular-season games at center between 1986 and 1993.

The Catch: He was often overlooked as an interior offensive lineman surrounded by stars at skill positions. He departed his abbreviated prime just as the Bills completed that unforgettable four-year run.

The Snapshot: A six-time AFL All-Star quarterback with Buffalo who was one of the faces of the franchise during its true glory days of the 1960s.

Claim to Fame: Quarterbacked Buffalo to back-to-back AFL titles and won the 1965 AFL MVP.

The Body of Work: The only championship-winning quarterback in Bills history, he posted a 43-31-3 record over seven seasons in Buffalo. Kemp remains fourth in team history in passing yards.

The Catch: It was a short-lived prime. During that Bills stretch, he threw nearly twice as many interceptions (132) as touchdowns (77) while the defense ran the show.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame wide receiver who was the offense's primary target for the vast majority of 15 seasons in Buffalo. He was the ultimate pass-catching weapon for Jim Kelly over the course of four consecutive Super Bowl appearances.

Claim to Fame: Buffalo's runaway all-time leader in receptions (941), receiving yards (13,095), and receiving touchdowns (86) was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

The Body of Work: A seven-time Pro Bowler, Reed served as Kelly's go-to receiver and consistently elevated his play in high-leverage playoff spots, punctuated by his legendary three-touchdown performance in " The Comeback ."

The Catch: He was never a first-team All-Pro. He had just one season with 10 touchdowns. Reed was never really the cream of the NFL receiver crop.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame guard who started 116 regular-season games for Buffalo from 1961 to 1969 and spent his entire career with the Bills in the AFL.

Claim to Fame: He was a first-team All-AFL selection in five consecutive seasons, two of which were championship campaigns

The Body of Work: He was enshrined in Canton in 1999 as an eight-time AFL All-Star who led the way for one of the best running games of that era. Shaw is also a member of the All-Time AFL Team.

The Catch: Like Kemp, he never played a snap in the NFL.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame guard who played eight seasons in Buffalo (1973-1979, 1985) and was O.J. Simpson's top blocker during the most dominant portion of his career.

Claim to Fame: A member of the 1970s All-Decade Team, DeLamielleure started all 14 games at right guard for the 1973 offensive line that blocked for the NFL's first 2,000-yard rusher.

The Body of Work: A 2003 Hall of Fame inductee, DeLamielleure was selected to five consecutive Pro Bowls as a Bill and earned three consecutive first-team All-Pro honors between 1975 and 1977. Between 1973 and 1975, Buffalo's ground game led the NFL in total rushing yards in three straight seasons, averaging 2,829 rushing yards and 22 rushing touchdowns per year.

The Catch: He was arguably still in his prime when he left the Bills for Cleveland in 1980. Who made whom better between DeLamielleure and Simpson is open to debate. Also, he and Simpson are the only players on this list who did very little winning in Buffalo.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame running back who played nine seasons in Buffalo (1969-1977), totaling 10,183 rushing yards and 69 scrimmage touchdowns across 112 games.

Claim to Fame: His 143.1 rushing yards per game in 1973 remains the highest qualified mark in NFL history by a considerable margin. That year, Simpson became the first player in NFL history to rush for 2,000 yards in a single season.

The Body of Work: The 1973 MVP wasn't a one-year wonder. He led the league in rushing yardage four times over five years, scoring 54 touchdowns between 1972 and 1976.

The Catch: He wasn't a major factor outside of that five-year window. He didn't contribute to a single playoff win in his NFL career.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame dual-threat back who served as the primary offensive engine for four straight AFC Championship teams, producing 18,393 combined regular-season and playoff yards from scrimmage and 108 total touchdowns.

Claim to Fame: Led the NFL in scrimmage yards for four consecutive seasons from 1989 through 1992 and won MVP in 1991.

The Body of Work: He was also a two-time first-team All-Pro and a five-time Pro Bowler. That alone doesn't get him into Simpson's range, but more than 2,000 yards and 21 touchdowns in his playoff career make a big difference.

The Catch: He was never quite as dominant as Simpson at their respective peaks, despite playing with far more offensive talent around him. It's a toss-up between the two, but Thomas was more of a big-moment presence.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame quarterback who ran Buffalo's no-huddle offense across 11 seasons, compiling 110 total wins (regular season and playoffs) and starting in four consecutive Super Bowls.

Claim to Fame: He's the only quarterback ever to lead his team to four consecutive conference championship victories.

The Body of Work: A five-time Pro Bowler and 1991 first-team All-Pro who led the NFL in passing touchdowns (33) and passer rating (92.3) that season. Kelly remains Buffalo's all-time passing leader with 35,467 yards and 237 touchdowns across 160 starts.

The Catch: Kelly's prime spanned five, maybe six seasons. Of course, he lost all four Super Bowls he played in while posting a mere 72.3 career playoff passer rating. Allen is also about to catch him in all-time touchdown passes and has already surpassed him in total passing/rushing scores.

The Snapshot: A franchise quarterback and four-time Pro Bowler whose 300-plus total passing and rushing touchdowns across his first eight seasons have helped Buffalo become the winningest team of the 2020s to date.

Claim to Fame: The 2024 MVP and 2026 MVP favorite has already rushed for more touchdowns than any quarterback in NFL history. He's the only player in league history to record five consecutive seasons with 40 or more total touchdowns.

The Body of Work: Pro Football Reference's Approximate V alue metric rates Allen as the single most valuable player in football since 2020. He hasn't missed a start since his rookie year in 2018. He holds Buffalo's single-season records for passing yards (4,544 in 2020) and passing touchdowns (37, that same year).

The Catch: The 30-year-old holds an 8-7 career postseason record and has not gotten the Bills to a Super Bowl.

The Snapshot: A Hall of Fame defensive end who played 15 seasons in Buffalo (1985-1999), starting 217 regular-season games and recording 171 sacks as a Bill.

Claim to Fame: The two-time Defensive Player of the Year is officially the NFL's all-time sack king with 200 in his career. He also added 14.5 in the playoffs, starting in four Super Bowls alongside Kelly, Thomas, Reed, Hull, Talley, Bennett and Tasker.

The Body of Work: Smith was named to both the 1980s and 1990s NFL All-Decade Teams. Only two players in modern NFL history have more first-team All-Pro honors than his eight.

The Catch: None. Smith is widely considered one of the best defensive players in the history of the sport. In this case, he pairs unmatched longevity with the highest defensive peak in Bills history.

articles.title: Week 5 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Flex, PPR Advice for Fringe Fantasy Football Stars
articles.summary: Week 5 brings the first bye weeks of the 2026 NFL season, and both the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs will be out of action. This means that several fantasy stars will be unavailable, in addition to those on the increasingly long list of injured players.
articles.body:
Week 5 brings the first bye weeks of the 2026 NFL season, and both the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs will be out of action. This means that several fantasy stars will be unavailable, in addition to those on the increasingly long list of injured players.

Many managers will be forced to rely on fringe starters this week, especially when it comes to filling out their flex positions. Fortunately, favorable matchups should allow several of them to come through.

Here, you'll find start/sit recommendations for some of this week's flex options based on past results, projected roles, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: Emanuel Wilson, RB, Seattle Seahawks

After placing rookie Jadarian Price on injured reserve, the Seattle Seahawks are running short on backfield options. Seattle did consider adding Joe Mixon to its practice squad and is probably in the market for RB help, but Emanuel Wilson is the new RB1 until further notice.

Wilson shined in the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. He caught three passes, tallied 120 scrimmage yards, and found the end zone twice. His floor is much lower this week against the San Francisco 49ers, though, as San Francisco has surrendered the seventh-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Still, Wilson's workload and PPR value should make him a solid flex option, even in a tough matchup. He should be good for double-digit fantasy points, at a minimum.

The list of other fringe RBs to consider for flex play includes:

Sit: Alvin Kamara, RB, New Orleans Saints

New Orleans Saints veteran Alvin Kamara became a must-add off the waiver wire when the Saints placed Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve. He came through for managers this past week, too, as he found the end zone twice against the Atlanta Falcons.

However, Kamara and the rest of the Saints' rushing attack have underwhelmed this season. Kamara has averaged 3.0 yards per carry on the year, and while he has a solid PPR floor (5 catches in Week 4), he's a very touchdown-dependent flex option.

There's a strong chance that Kamara won't find the end zone against the Minnesota Vikings this week. Minnesota has only given up a single rushing touchdown through four weeks and has surrendered the fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

Other RBs to avoid in the flex this week:

Start: Carnell Tate, WR, Tennessee Titans

Rookie receiver and fourth overall pick Carnell Tate largely underwhelmed through the first two weeks of the season. Of course, the winless Tennessee Titans struggled early to get their offense out of neutral.

Tate has started to play up to his draft status over the past couple of weeks, though, and is finally looking like a reliable flex option. He had six catches for 58 yards in Week 3 and just put up nine catches on 12 targets for 145 yards against the Baltimore Ravens.

Presumably, the Titans will continue funneling the ball to Tate, who has a favorable matchup against the rival Houston Texans this week. While Houston's defense was a force a year ago, it has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing receivers than any other team.

Other WRs to consider in the flex in Week 5:

Sit: Matthew Golden, WR, Green Bay Packers

Second-year receiver Matthew Golden has started to shine for the Green Bay Packers, and he's managed to reach double-digit fantasy points in three of his four outings this season. However, he still isn't the sort of high-volume receiver that makes him a must-start in any given matchup.

While Golden did find the end zone in Week 4, he caught just three passes and finished with 11.7 fantasy points. He projects as a touchdown-dependent option against the rival Chicago Bears this week, which is far less than ideal.

The Bears have actually been pretty stingy against opposing receivers and have surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to the position. The Packers' offense has looked out of sync for most of the season, which leaves Golden with a very questionable PPR floor.
