articles.title: Latest NFL Odds and Picks Factoring in New Weather Forecasts for Week 5 Schedule
articles.summary: We're officially one month into the 2026 NFL season, and we're finally beginning to get an idea of which teams are good and which are not—the league has five winless teams and only three undefeated squads.
articles.body:
We're officially one month into the 2026 NFL season, and we're finally beginning to get an idea of which teams are good and which are not—the league has five winless teams and only three undefeated squads.

Of course, this doesn't mean that every game moving forward will be easily predictable. On the contrary, it feels like most teams have a chance to win on any given day this season.

With fall now in full effect, the weather is becoming equally unpredictable and will start to impact games.

Here, you'll find a look at the information you need to know for Week 5, including predictions and forecast information from The Weather Channel .

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+8.5) at Dallas Cowboys (Retractable Roof)

Philadelphia Eagles (+6.5) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)

Cincinnati Bengals (-7.5) at Miami Dolphins

Las Vegas Raiders (+3.5) at New England Patriots

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 15 MPH, High of 87°F

Minnesota Vikings (-1.5) at New Orleans Saints (Dome)

Cleveland Browns (+1.5) at New York Jets

Forecast: Showers Possible, Winds up to 15MPH, High of 69°F

Indianapolis Colts (+1.5) at Pittsburgh Steelers

Houston Texans (-6.5) at Tennessee Titans

New York Giants (+4.5) at Washington Commanders

Chicago Bears (-2.5) at Green Bay Packers

Denver Broncos (-3.5) at Los Angeles Chargers (Dome)

Detroit Lions (-4.5) at Arizona Cardinals (Retractable Roof)

Forecast: Scattered Thunderstorms, Winds up to 15MPH, High of 88°F

San Francisco 49ers (+3) at Seattle Seahawks

Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Atlanta Falcons (Retractable Roof)

Forecast: Rain Showers Possible, Winds up to 15MPH, Low of 59°F

Buffalo Bills (+2.5) at Los Angeles Rams (Dome)

Bye Week: Carolina Panthers, New England Patriots

While playoff races are nowhere near close to being decided, Week 5 will be a pivotal week for several teams. Five franchises enter the week still in search of their first wins.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are one of them, and they'll open the schedule against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday night. On paper, this feels like a major mismatch in favor of the Cowboys, especially with Tampa starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels—Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated thumb.

However, Dallas' defense remains a major liability, and Daniels' scrambling ability could make the Week 5 opener more exciting, and closer, than expected.

Sunday's action will open with a London morning game between the surging Jacksonville Jaguars and the injured Philadelphia Eagles. The list of injured Eagles now includes Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Tank Bigsby, Cam Jurgens, Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, and Quinyon Mitchell.

Sunday afternoon will bring a battle of winless teams when the Houston Texans clash with the Tennessee Titans. Barring the unfortunate event of a tie, at least one winless squad should get in the win column this week.

The Miami Dolphins will have a chance to get their first win against the Cincinnati Bengals, who saw star receivers Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) injured in Week 4. The Los Angeles Chargers will try to get their first victory in the late afternoon against the banged-up Denver Broncos.

Denver saw standouts Pat Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Pat Bryant suffer injuries in Week 4.

Sunday night's game will feature the Atlanta Falcons, who just embarrassed the New Orleans Saints in prime time on Monday. The Baltimore Ravens could still present a challenge, but they're unlikely to have star quarterback Lamar Jackson.

Jackson is dealing with an ankle injury and could end up missing multiple games, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

The Week 5 slate will end with a thriller between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. Buffalo is coming off its first loss of the season and will test a Rams team that has fallen short of expectations thus far. However, Los Angeles has Puka Nacua back and appeared to find a spark in the second half against the Eagles this past Sunday.

Weather may not be a major factor this week, especially since the Falcons and Arizona Cardinals can close off their stadiums if rain persists. Rain could have an impact on the NFC East showdown between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders, however.

In all, it's shaping up to be a fun week that, if this year's trends hold, will bring another round of surprising finishes.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Davis Webb's Hot Seat as Broncos Playcaller Under Sean Payton Amid Struggles
articles.summary: Davis Webb's status as the Denver Broncos' offensive playcaller reportedly could be in jeopardy if significant improvement is not shown in the near future.
articles.body:
Davis Webb's status as the Denver Broncos' offensive playcaller reportedly could be in jeopardy if significant improvement is not shown in the near future.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , "a lot of people" in the NFL believe Broncos head coach Sean Payton "won't wait too much longer" to take back the offensive playcalling duties from Webb.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler added that although he expects Webb to be given "more time," a change could be made if Denver's offense does not start living up to expectations.

Payton called the Broncos' offensive plays over each of his first three seasons as head coach, and he enjoyed solid success in that role with the 10th-ranked scoring offense in 2024 and the 10th-ranked unit in total offense last season.

The veteran head coach and one-time Super Bowl champion with the New Orleans Saints seemingly pushed all the right buttons for quarterback Bo Nix, who threw for 3,775 yards, 29 touchdowns and 12 interceptions as a rookie in 2024, and followed that up with 3,931 yards, 25 touchdowns and 11 picks last season.

If not for Nix suffering a season-ending ankle injury in the Broncos' AFC Divisional Round playoff game win over the Buffalo Bills, they may very well have gone to the Super Bowl, as they mustered only seven points with backup Jarrett Stidham under center in a 10-7 loss to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game.

Webb, who served as Denver's quarterbacks coach from 2023 to 2025, as well as their offensive passing game coordinator last season, was a hot coaching commodity this past offseason as a potential head coach and offensive coordinator.

In order to keep Webb in the fold, Denver promoted him to OC and gave him offensive playcalling responsibilities.

Early returns on that decision have not been good, as the 2-2 Broncos are 27th in the NFL in total offense and 27th in scoring offense with just 18.5 points per game.

On top of that, Nix is trending toward the worst season of his young career, as he is completing a career-low 60.0 percent of his passes for 819 yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions through four games.

Part of the issue could be the tough defensive matchups the Broncos have drawn thus far with games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers.

Things could perhaps get a bit easier against the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, and there will be a great deal of pressure on Webb to produce a strong offensive performance in that game.

articles.title: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes' and  1587 Prime legal fight intensifies as their bid to dismiss the lawsuit faces strong opposition
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are facing a legal fight over one of their biggest ventures away from the NFL.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are facing a legal fight over one of their biggest ventures away from the NFL. The Kansas City Chiefs stars are trying to have a trademark lawsuit tied to their 1587 Prime steakhouse dismissed, but the company behind 1587 Sneakers is pushing back. The dispute centers on the “1587” name, which both sides say has different roots and uses. With arguments now filed on both sides, the case has added another layer of attention to the restaurant launched by two of Kansas City’s most recognizable athletes.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce seek dismissal in 1587 Prime lawsuitThe dispute began in February when 1587 Sneakers sued Mahomes, Kelce and others in federal court in New York. The sneaker company argues that the use of “1587” by the Kansas City restaurant could confuse customers and affect its brand.The number has a clear connection to the Chiefs stars. 1587 Prime combines Mahomes’ No. 15 with Kelce’s No. 87. The restaurant opened in September 2025 after the players partnered with Noble 33.1587 Sneakers, however, says its business predates the restaurant. The company began selling footwear and clothing in 2023 and later sought federal trademark protection for “1587” in the clothing category.The restaurant’s trademark application is separate and covers bar and restaurant services. That distinction is now central to the legal dispute.The sneaker company wants the restaurant to stop using the 1587 Prime name and seeks damages. It also claims customers have contacted the sneaker brand believing the two businesses are connected.Mahomes and Kelce have taken a different position. Their lawyers filed a motion on July 3 asking the court to dismiss the claims against the two athletes with prejudice. Their legal team has argued that the players do not control the restaurant and do not have the necessary connection to New York for the claims to proceed against them there.1587 Sneakers pushes back against Mahomes and KelceThe sneaker company responded on Aug. 4, challenging the attempt to separate Mahomes and Kelce from the restaurant and its branding.The filing argues that the athletes were not simply celebrity promoters but played a meaningful role in creating the identity behind 1587 Prime."Defendants Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes seek dismissal by recasting themselves as two distant celebrities that are mere promotional 'pretty faces' of the alleged infringing enterprise with no New York ties," the filing reads. "The record shows otherwise."As sufficiently alleged in the operative complaint, both Defendants played an active personal role as the 'moving forces' of the at-issue mark as '1587' was approved and constructed from their respective football jersey numbers: 15 and 87."For now, the lawsuit remains unresolved. The court will ultimately decide whether the claims against Mahomes and Kelce can continue, leaving the future of the 1587 Prime name tied to a legal battle far removed from the football field.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mel Kiper Jr. Reveals New Top Prospects for 2027 NFL Draft amid Jeremiah Smith Heisman Hype
articles.summary: Having solidified his status as the Heisman frontrunner, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is also regarded as the best player in the 2027 NFL draft class by ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.
articles.body:
Having solidified his status as the Heisman frontrunner , Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is also regarded as the best player in the 2027 NFL draft class by ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.

In the latest episode of First Draft (starts at 3:50 mark), Kiper revealed his top five players in the 2027 draft as things currently stand with Smith at No. 1 overall.

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 5 📋

Other players ranked by Kiper include Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (No. 6) and Florida running back Jadan Baugh (No. 10). He also Notre Dame wide receiver Jordan Faison and Clemson cornerback Ashton Hampton.

Smith entered the season generally regarded as the best player in the country. He has only improved his stock with at least 150 receiving yards in four of Ohio State's first five games.

The worst performance for Smith so far was an 85-yard outing against Kent State in a 59-3 win for the Buckeyes. He has had back-to-back games with more than 200 yards since then.

Based on the current standings , the Houston Texans would have the top pick in the 2027 draft. Given the talent at quarterback, their most-likely path would be to trade down with a team looking for a signal-caller.

However, the Texans putting Smith in an offense with C.J. Stroud and Nico Collins plus the defensive talent they already have in place would be an appealing option.

If Smith were to be the No. 1 pick, he would join Keyshawn Johnson in 1996 and Irving Fryar in 1984 as the only wide receivers to be taken with the top overall selection in the common draft era (since 1967).

Comparing Kiper's current ranking to his preseason list from Aug. 17, the two biggest changes are Dante Moore and Arch Manning no longer being the top quarterbacks.

Kiper noted he would "maybe" have both Manning and Moore of them near the bottom of a top-25 ranking right now.

Those two have been replaced at the top of the quarterback group by Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Miami's Darian Mensah.

Mestemaker, who is in his first season at Oklahoma State after transferring from North Texas, has thrown for 1,271 yards and 11 touchdowns in four games. His highest-profile game was a 39-31 win over Moore and Oregon on Sept. 12.

Mensah is off to a historic start in terms of accuracy with an 84.2 completion percentage through five games. He has nearly as many incompletions (21) as touchdown passes (15) this season and has yet to throw an interception.

articles.title: Falcons Troll 12 Teams to Hype Bijan Robinson, Drake London's Stats in Comparison
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons' star duo of Bijan Robinson and Drake London has been more productive than a dozen entire NFL offenses through the last two weeks.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons' star duo of Bijan Robinson and Drake London has been more productive than a dozen entire NFL offenses through the last two weeks.

Robinson and London have racked up a combined 650 scrimmage yards in a Week 3 win at the Green Bay Packers and Week 4 victory at the New Orleans Saints.

The Falcons pointed out Wednesday this marked more production over the span than that recorded by the Denver Broncos, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Indianapolis Colts, Washington Commanders, Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles, New York Giants, New York Jets, Green Bay Packers, Houston Texans, Tennessee Titans and Minnesota Vikings.

The run started Sept. 24 when Robinson racked up 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns, while London made nine catches for another 194 yards in a 34-14 win over the Packers.

Robinson then ran 19 times with 145 yards and two touchdowns, while London made five catches for 96 receiving yards in a 45-24 victory Oct. 5 at the Saints.

London now leads the NFL in most receiving yards without a receiving touchdown so far this season, per PFF .

This run for Robinson and London coincides with the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. from the left knee injury he suffered in Week 11 of the 2025 season.

After going 0-2 with Cooper Rush under center, the Falcons have improved to 2-2 since Penix's return.

The Falcons will hope Penix can continue driving his team's resurgence, while London will continue looking for his first receiving touchdown of the season, when the Falcons return home Sunday for a Week 5 matchup against the visiting Baltimore Ravens.

articles.title: Kyle Juszczyk's Fine For Chugging Celebration Rescinded by NFL After 49ers FB's Appeal
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk has successfully appealed his fine for celebrating a Week 2 touchdown against the Miami Dolphins by miming chugging a drink.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk has successfully appealed his fine for celebrating a Week 2 touchdown against the Miami Dolphins by miming chugging a drink.

The NFL rescinded the $14,926 fine Wednesday after concluding Juszczyk "was simulating drinking a juice box, not a beer," according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The league noted Juszczyk "stated that the fine is hypocritical with the amount of Bud Light sponsorships surrounding the NFL," per Schefter.

NFL suspends two refs for 'unprofessional conduct'

The initial penalty was in response to Juszczyk's touchdown celebration Sept. 20 in the third quarter of a win over the Dolphins.

The NFL sent Juszczyk a letter after the game saying his "imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste," per Schefter .

Juszczyk told reporters he intended to appeal the decision alongside a $20,033 Week 1 fine for unnecessary roughness and use of his helmet in a Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Rams, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner .

"I don't know how else to say it. I wasn't drinking beer in my celebration... when I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice, and it's been that way for years," Juszczyk told reporters after the Dolphins game (h/t broadcaster Ben Ross).

Juszczyk later added he felt even a beer-drinking celebration would not have been worthy of fine because of the NFL's endorsement deals with Bud Light, including the naming rights for a section of the concourse at Levi's Stadium (h/t 95.7 The Game).

Juszczyk appealed his fines in a Sept. 29 meeting with NFL representatives. He said later that week he thought things were "going to work out okay," per Wagoner .

The rescinding of the fine isn't the only good news Juszczyk has received recently. Schefter reported Monday the knee injury suffered by Juszczyk in a Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos was not a season-ending issue but rather a sprain and bone bruise expected to sideline him for two to three weeks.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday Juszczyk's absence could create more opportunities for tight end Brayden Willis.

Willis will be expected to join Luke Farrell and George Kittle in covering for the Niners' injured star fullback when the team works on holding onto its NFC West lead without Juszczyk this Sunday at the Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: NFL Insiders Sound Off on Brian Flores, Declan Doyle, Top Potential HC Candidates
articles.summary: Through the first four games of the 2026 NFL season, multiple potential candidates have emerged for future head coaching jobs.
articles.body:
Through the first four games of the 2026 NFL season, multiple potential candidates have emerged for future head coaching jobs.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano discussed the coordinators from around the league who are getting early looks for potential openings, most notably highlighting Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores.

"Obviously, what Brian Flores is doing with Minnesota's defense is incredible, and he should get another shot at a head coaching job at some point," Graziano stated.

Flores served as head coach of the Miami Dolphins for three seasons from 2019 to 2021. While his previous experience could set him apart from other candidates, Graziano cautioned that "there are other factors at play there, as we all know. I'm starting to wonder if Flores has any shot being a head coach while his lawsuit against the league is still pending."

As for candidates with no prior head coaching experience, Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is the frontrunner to be elevated next offseason.

"He has brought new elements to the Baltimore attack, and Lamar Jackson seems to really enjoy playing for him. Word is that Doyle was highly impressive on the OC interview trail a year ago, not only in Baltimore but in Philadelphia, too," Fowler explained. "The league is always looking for ascending offensive minds to help build with a young quarterback, and the 30-year-old Doyle fits that mold. He has the poised demeanor to be a head coach."

Graziano pointed to Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, whose unit leads the NFL with six turnovers this season.

"The Jaguars look as good as any team in the league right now, and the program has come together very quickly in its second year under head coach Liam Coen. When teams look for head coaching candidates, they look to the organizations that are doing a lot of winning," Graziano stated. "Campanile's defense is fourth in the NFL in EPA, and only the Vikings are allowing fewer points per game than the Jaguars' 13.3. Trevor Lawrence and Coen's offense are obviously operating at a high level right now. But if Jacksonville keeps this up and repeats as AFC South champs, which is looking extremely possible right now, it'll have a lot to do with the way things have come together on defense."

"Yes, Campanile has proof of concept. He was a finalist for Arizona's job this winter. His teams play physical football," Fowler responded. "Both of Jacksonville's coordinators, Campanile and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski, should be in the mix yet again. They have a good thing going in North Florida."

The list doesn't stop there, as teams like the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons have impressed early on, strengthening the resumes of their respective coordinators.

"What Carolina offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is doing with Bryce Young will be hard to ignore. The Panthers have jumped from 26th to first in passing offense. He has Young playing fast and with confidence. That will get noticed by front offices and owners," Fowler stated. "Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees is on a nice stretch, as is Dallas OC Klayton Adams."

"Atlanta is a fun story in the early going, and defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is getting love around the league for the job he's doing with a unit that's short-handed up front," Graziano added. "He finished the 2024 season as the Jets' interim head coach. That obviously didn't go well, but Ulbrich is extremely well-liked and respected around the league and could get looks if the Falcons have a big season."

articles.title: New Jayden Daniels Rumors Update Injury Status for Commanders vs. Giants After Elbow Dislocation
articles.summary: After suffering a dislocated left elbow in Week 2, Washington Commanders star quarterback Jayden Daniels reportedly could have the chance to return for the team's Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants on Sunday.
articles.body:
After suffering a dislocated left elbow in Week 2, Washington Commanders star quarterback Jayden Daniels reportedly could have the chance to return for the team's Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants on Sunday.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler provided an optimistic update on Daniels' recovery from his second left elbow dislocation in the last year.

"The outlook for the Commanders' Jayden Daniels potentially playing this week against the Giants is positive," Fowler stated. "The key, I'm told, is having him in practice in full. Limited participation likely won't be enough. If he's a full go in practice by, say, Friday, he'll get the green light."

Daniels traveled with the Commanders for their Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts in the NFL London Game, but he was ultimately ruled out after being limited in practice all week.

Marcus Mariota, who started last week's game, is sidelined after suffering a sprained MCL against the Colts. Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis entered in his place and would start on Sunday if Daniels isn't cleared.

If Daniels can get through practice this week, though, he could be under center when the Commanders (1-3) take on the NFC East-leading Giants (3-1) on Sunday.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Agrees to Vikings Contract After Giants Release, Full Details Announced
articles.summary: Following his release from the New York Giants, Odell Beckham Jr. has found a new home with the Minnesota Vikings, the team announced on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Following his release from the New York Giants, Odell Beckham Jr. has found a new home with the Minnesota Vikings, the team announced on Wednesday.

Beckham will initially join Minnesota's practice squad while Justin Jefferson continues to nurse an ankle injury.

Beckham signed with the Giants in June, setting up a reunion between him and the team he spent his best years with. He made the 53-man roster ahead of the season, but it quickly became apparent that he wasn't going to be a big part of the offensive game plan.

Beckham played just a handful of snaps and had just one target through the Giants' first few games, and the team ultimately released him on Sept. 29. The decision to part ways reportedly was mutual as Beckham eyed a bigger role elsewhere.

At 33 years old, Beckham isn't the All-Pro caliber player he once was, but he has the potential to make an impact with his new squad.

Beckham didn't play during the 2025 season and got limited reps with the Miami Dolphins in 2024, but he hauled in 35 catches for 565 yards and three touchdowns with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, and he'll look to have that kind of production with Minnesota.

The Vikings are 4-0 and have a matchup with the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.

articles.title: Colts' Carlie Irsay-Gordon Responds to Viral Videos, Explains Why She Takes Notes on Sideline
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has drawn attention for her presence on the sidelines during games, but there's a reason for it.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has drawn attention for her presence on the sidelines during games, but there's a reason for it.

While speaking to Bridget Condon of Front Office Sports Tonight , Irsay-Gordon said she's simply trying to educate herself about the team's football operations and coaching approach.

"I like to say on a good day I have like a fifth-grade reading level understanding of the game and just the basic concepts of what we're trying to do, depending on the week and depending on our opponent and depending on the situation," Irsay-Gordon told Condon . "But I think, then, it just helps to understand and to ask questions because I think one of the things, in my opinion, like being a good leader is about listening, really to understand. And I think that's what the best teams do."

Irsay-Gordon took over as the Colts' principal owner and CEO last year following the death of her father, Jim Irsay. Her sister, Kalen Jackson, serves as owner and chief brand officer, and her other sister, Casey Foyt, is also an owner and executive vice president. All three of them had been owners and vice chairs of the team for 14 seasons before taking on their current roles.

However, it's Irsay-Gordon who has become a fixture at Colts games as she tries to help rebuild a franchise that has gone five straight years without a playoff appearance. Indianapolis improved to 2-2 this year with Sunday's 30-13 win over the Washington Commanders in the NFL London Game, but Irsay-Gordon's spot on the sideline drew some criticism.

"I'm not going to tiptoe around this anymore, right? And I know it's been a topic the last couple weeks. I think the owner on the sidelines taking notes is f--king nuts," The Ringer's Bill Simmons said on his podcast on Monday. "I think it's nuts. … I think it's bonkers. I can't believe she does this. And I can't believe people in her life haven't talked her out of it."

Still, Irsay-Gordon maintained that she's learning to adjust to her new role as principal owner, and she acknowledged that the increased scrutiny comes with the job.

"With our dad passing away and kind of now me, you know, the title changed a lot of what I was doing," she told Condon. " … [But] what I'm still doing isn't any different. So I think that's been something… to be more mindful of, that now people might be paying more attention to what I'm doing."

The Colts will be back in action in Week 5 in a road matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2), so it will be interesting to see if Irsay-Gordon changes her approach on game day.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Jerry Jeudy, Josh Sweat, More Possible 2026 Trade Deadline Targets
articles.summary: One month away from the NFL trade deadline, teams are monitoring the status of several players who could end up being difference-makers for playoff contenders.
articles.body:
One month away from the NFL trade deadline, teams are monitoring the status of several players who could end up being difference-makers for playoff contenders.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Jerry Jeudy, Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack, Jermaine Johnson II and Will McDonald IV are among the key names receiving trade buzz after the first four weeks of the regular season.

From that group, Mack would make the most sense as a trade candidate. The Los Angeles Chargers don't appear to be going anywhere amid an 0-4 start; he is 35 and will become a free agent at the end of this season.

Jeudy would fit the bill of a clear trade candidate because Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have given the Cleveland Browns plenty of pass-catching options.

However, with the Browns off to a 3-1 start, subtracting a key player from their roster might not be what they are looking to do. Their offensive system also relies on three-receiver sets.

Per Sumer Sports , the Browns' 64.2 percent rate of running 11 personnel is the eighth-highest in the NFL right now. Jeudy is also owed $13.5 million next season and has just five catches for 62 yards so far in 2026.

Mack and Johnson, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, might be the easiest to trade given their current contracts. McDonald is owed a fully-guaranteed $14.5 million in 2027 on the final season of his rookie contract.

Even though Mack is at an age when his performance would normally be in decline, he remains a bright spot in an otherwise disastrous Chargers season. The nine-time Pro Bowler has five tackles for loss, five quarterback hits and three sacks in four games.

The Arizona Cardinals are in a difficult spot with Sweat because his contract runs through 2028. He has cap hits of $23.6 million in each of the next two seasons, though there's no guaraneed money left on his deal after 2026.

Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort was s aying as recently as August they had no plans to trade Sweat. A 1-3 start to the season might lead them to change their approach.

Sweat only has one sack through four games, but he recorded 12 sacks during the 2025 season.

Teams will start putting together their trade plans soon, if they haven't started already, since the deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s Fantasy Outlook with Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson After Vikings Contract
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings added to their already talented wide receiver corps Wednesday by signing Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings added to their already talented wide receiver corps Wednesday by signing Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad.

If OBJ is eventually elevated to the 53-man roster, he will become part of a receiver room that includes Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and 2025 third-round pick Tai Felton.

Given that Beckham is starting on the practice squad, is not guaranteed to get a call-up and would be behind three or four other capable wideouts on Minnesota's depth chart, it would not be advisable to count on him for any modicum of fantasy football production.

Jefferson is the Vikings' unquestioned No. 1 receiver and go-to target when healthy, although he did miss last week's win against the Miami Dolphins with an ankle injury.

However, head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters it would not be a long-term issue, which suggests he could be back as soon as Week 5.

Addison is the established WR2 in O'Connell's offense, and although Jennings has just two catches for nine yards in the three games he has appeared in this season, he has a history of success, registering 975 receiving yards in 2024 and scoring nine touchdowns last season with the San Francisco 49ers.

With Jefferson out, quarterback Kyler Murray made tight end T.J. Hockenson his favorite target, as Hockenson racked up 13 catches for 119 yards against Miami.

On top of that, running back Aaron Jones is a capable pass-catcher out of the backfield, as his nine receptions rank fourth on the team.

All of that is to say the Vikings have no shortage of offensive weapons, and barring additional injuries, Beckham likely wouldn't be anything more than a veteran presence and a modest contributor.

OBJ was once among the NFL's best wide receivers during his time with the New York Giants, averaging 96 receptions for 1,374 yards and nearly 12 touchdowns over his first three NFL seasons from 2014 to 2016, and earning three Pro Bowl selections during that stretch.

However, Beckham has never quite been the same player as he once was since tearing his ACL during the Los Angeles Rams' Super Bowl win over the Cincinnati Bengals to close out the 2021 season.

The Giants brought him back to the Big Apple this past offseason and he made the initial 53-man roster, which was one of the biggest feel-good stories of the preseason.

Beckham did not record a catch in three games to start the regular season, though, and the Giants parted ways with him on Sept. 29.

While the soon-to-be 34-year-old Beckham has found a new landing spot, he figures to serve as depth rather than an important part of the Minnesota offense.

articles.title: Justin Herbert’s Chargers job suddenly looks vulnerable after Cam Newton admits benching him could be the answer
articles.summary: Cam Newton thinks the Los Angeles Chargers should seriously consider sitting Justin Herbert.
articles.body: Cam Newton thinks the Los Angeles Chargers should seriously consider sitting Justin Herbert. The former MVP made the case on his 4th & 1 podcast after Los Angeles fell to 0-4 with a Week 4 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Herbert has 816 passing yards, four touchdowns and six interceptions this season, and Newton says the quarterback is a big reason the team cannot win. The comments put Herbert's job in an unusual spotlight for a player on a large contract. They also raise a harder question for head coach Jim Harbaugh.Why does Cam Newton think the Chargers should bench Justin Herbert?Newton did not soften it. “We need to have a case study out for him. Maybe he needs to put his hind parts on the bench,” he said. Then he got more direct. “Justin is the reason why the Los Angeles Chargers are losing.”He backed that up with numbers. “His passer rating is 70. Completion percentage 59%. His QBR is amongst the worst of all quarterbacks, at 27,” Newton said. Pro Football Network's quarterback impact metric agrees on the direction, placing Herbert last in the league at 61.4.The contract is the other half of his argument. Newton pointed to a “franchise quarterback with a huge contract,” and then to a team with no wins. In his view, that deal makes Herbert the common denominator, the one who is supposed to be the difference. “Well, we need a difference made, right? Justin Herbert ain't getting the job done,” he said.His fix is bold. Newton wants Herbert to “control + alt + delete and start all over, and reboot the whole system.” He also offered an example, saying a benching seemed to spark better play from Bryce Young.Would benching Justin Herbert actually fix the Chargers?Maybe, but it is not that simple. A quarterback is the easiest name to blame when a team is 0-4. Pass protection, play calling and the defense all affect those numbers. Nothing in the reference suggests Harbaugh is planning a switch.Still, Newton knows something about being the face of a struggling team, and his point has a human side. A short stay on the sideline can give a passer time to see the game differently. For some players, it works. For others, it hurts confidence and makes things worse.The risk is higher for Herbert because of who he is. He is not a young player fighting to keep a job. Sitting him would send a loud message about the whole team, not only about him.So the real question is what the Chargers do next. An 0-4 record leaves little room, and Herbert's numbers will get a long look this week. articles.title: Travis Kelce Reacts to Viral Photo of Taylor Swift-Themed Hay Bale Decoration
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce has some questions about the design choices involved in building hay bale renditions of himself and his wife Taylor Swift.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce has some questions about the design choices involved in building hay bale renditions of himself and his wife Taylor Swift.

Kelce reacted with his brother Jason Kelce on Wednesday's episode of their New Heights podcast to a viral photo of stacked bales labeled Haylor Swift and Travis Kelc-hay.

"Why'd they have to make my wife cross-eyed, that's all I'm asking," Kelce said around the 9:20 mark of the podcast.

When Jason Kelce suggested Swift's hay doppelgänger might be about to sneeze, Kelce laughed, "She does go cross-eyed before she sneezes."

Kelce and Swift were married this July in New York City.

Swift has been in attendance for two Chiefs home games this season, including a Week 2 matchup during which she pointed to her wedding ring after her husband scored a touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts.

Kelce and the Chiefs are currently on a Week 5 bye before returning for their next home game Oct. 18 against the Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill's Updated NFL Landing Spots After Odell Beckham Jr. Signs Vikings Contract
articles.summary: With Odell Beckham Jr. is back in the NFL following his abbreviated stint with the New York Giants, the veteran receiver market will turn its attention to Tyreek Hill as he looks to return to the field coming off a major knee injury.
articles.body:
With Odell Beckham Jr. is back in the NFL following his abbreviated stint with the New York Giants, the veteran receiver market will turn its attention to Tyreek Hill as he looks to return to the field coming off a major knee injury.

Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz , Beckham is signing with the Minnesota Vikings. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the three-time Pro Bowler will be on the practice squad.

Hill has already been linked in a potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs following injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton in Sunday's win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Other receiver-needy teams that also have playoff aspirations at this point include the Raiders and New England Patriots.

Drew Rosenhaus, Hill's agent, told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday he was planning to negotiate with teams about the veteran wideout that same day.

Despite potential interest from other clubs, Rapaport said it would be a "surprise" if Hill ends up anywhere other than Kansas City.

The Patriots are going to get pass-catching help when A.J. Brown returns from the sprained ankle that has kept him out since Week 1. He is currently on injured reserve, so the earliest he could play is Week 6 against the New York Jets.

Brown is reportedly pushing to return as soon as he is eligible.

There might have been more urgency from the Patriots to make another move if they continued on their trajectory through the first three games, but Sunday's win over the Buffalo Bills quieted some of the concerns.

Efton Chism III, who caught the game-winning touchdown against Buffalo, is also earning more playing time. His 34 offensive snaps were eight more than he had in the first two games combined.

The Raiders' 3-1 start push them to make additions prior to the trade deadline. They need more help on the outside with Tre Tucker as the only receiver on the team with at least 200 receiving yards.

Among wide receivers on the Raiders' roster, Cody White is second on the team with five catches for 64 yards. The offense runs through tight end Brock Bowers, who is second on the team with 202 receiving yards despite missing two games.

It's not a surprise the Chiefs would be viewed as overwhelming favorites to sign Hill. His familiarity with Andy Reid's scheme and quarterback Patrick Mahomes would make it easy to get acclimated back into the league.

The big question hovering over Hill's playing career right now is, what will he look like coming off a major injury at the age of 32? He dislocated his left knee, tore the ACL and LCL last season with the Miami Dolphins.

Hill is reportedly targeting November for his return to game action, though he would presumably likely want to be signed ahead of time so he can practice with a team.

In four games with Miami last season prior to the injury, Hill had 265 yards and one touchdown on 21 catches. He spent his first six seasons in Kansas City, racking up 6,630 receiving yards and 56 receiving touchdowns in 91 games.

articles.title: B/R 99: Ranking the 99 Best NFL Rookies After Week 4
articles.summary: The Bleacher Report Scouting Department reconvened as the NFL season rounds the quarter mark of the 2026 campaign to see how the league's rookies are performing. At this juncture, one thing is certain: Defensive rookies are contributing at a much higher level.
articles.body:
The Bleacher Report Scouting Department reconvened as the NFL season rounds the quarter mark of the 2026 campaign to see how the league's rookies are performing. At this juncture, one thing is certain: Defensive rookies are contributing at a much higher level.

In fact, nine of the top 10 first-year performances so far are found on the defensive side of the ball, including each of the top four.

These rankings are based on what's been seen to date, with some projection where each individual's respective season can still go. For example, this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, has yet to see the field because veteran Kirk Cousins has played well. Mendoza is still found among these rankings, albeit much lower than initially anticipated, based on his upside and the expectation that he'll eventually play.

Some projection is necessary, because fewer than 75 rookies have played at least 100 snaps so far. But those first-year players at the top of the list have already made an impact.

Player evaluations, grades and write-ups were done by Bleacher Report NFL scouts Damian Parson (QB/WR/RB/FB), Brandon Thorn (OL), Matt Holder (EDGE, LB, DL) and Dan Harms (TE, CB, Safety) .

Anything can happen once an NFL season starts.

For example, the Los Angeles Chargers' Jake Slaughter, who was originally slated to compete at left guard, was forced back to center because veteran Tyler Biadasz suffered a season-ending knee injury. Despite being a natural center and a second-round draft pick, Slaughter has struggled to adjust.

For more was expected from wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., whom the New York Jets drafted with this year's 30th overall pick. Unfortunately, the recent first-rounder continues to deal with an ankle injury.

Conversely, undrafted free agents Aaron Hall and Wydett Williams Jr. have exceeded expectations, with Hall starting one game and Williams experiencing increased usage through each week of play.

The San Francisco 49ers' De'Zhaun Stribling was easily the most impressive rookie among this bunch, but he's currently on injured reserve with the possibility of returning later this season.

Keep scrolling to explore the next tier.

Our first top-10 draft pick appears on the list, albeit as a pure projection.

The New Orleans Saints' Jordyn Tyson has yet to play a meaningful NFL down because of a lingering hamstring issue. He's not expected back until Week 7 " at the earliest ." However, his eventual return should create excitement since the Saints already field the league's top-four passing offense. Tyson's addition will only make the unit even more dynamic. He's not the only one to expect increased usage once he's in the starting lineup.

Markel Bell will likely take over as the Philadelphia Eagles' full-time starting right tackle after Lane Johnson's retirement. The Miami produce already started in Week 4, with the potential to become the Eagles' long-term replacement.

Similarly, Chicago Bears cornerback Malik Muhammad continues to grow into bigger role and flourish as the team's primary nickel defender.

The Indianapolis Colts' Bryce Boettcher has garnered more playing time than the team's top draft pick, CJ Allen. To be fair, Allen has dealt with injuries and lost far too many practice reps. The second-rounder was previously viewed as a projected starter at middle linebacker and the Colts' defensive playcaller, with top-10 rookie potential. Instead, his teammate has contributed more.

Significant upside exists among this particular tier.

As mentioned, Allen was held in high regard entering the season and could eventually become the heart of the Colts' defense once he's fully healthy and up to speed. He's yet to make an impact, though, hence the drastic slide down the rankings.

The Arizona Cardinals will eventually turn to third-round quarterback Carson Beck unless something drastically changes after a 1-3 start. The Cardinals are now 2-14 since Jacoby Brissett was anointed QB1. Arizona's front office and coaching eventually need to see what Beck can do before making a decision at quarterback next offseason.

The Philadelphia Eagles traded up in the first round for wide receiver Makai Lemon. Ten catches in his first four games, while failing to contribute more than 29 yards in any of those contests, doesn't create excitement for a top-20 draft pick. However, DeVonta Smith is currently dealing with a hamstring injury. Thus, Lemon should see increased usage and targets in the coming weeks.

Keldric Faulk was viewed as a developmental option when the Tennessee Titans' traded back into the first round to acquire his services. The defensive lineman already showed improvement over the last three weeks and should continue his upward trend as the season progress, which is the primary goal for any rookie.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Reuben Bain Jr. and Seattle Seahawks' Jadarian Price immediately jump to the forefront among these names. Both were viewed as top-six rookie projections by the B/R Scouting Dept. entering this season. Both have disappointed, albeit injuries played a factor.

Bain didn't look anywhere near the same explosive defender he put on tape as part of the Miami Hurricanes. Some blamed it on arm length. Others looked at an underwhelming pass-rush plan. While both may have played a factor, Bain has also dealt with shoulder and groin injuries, which caused this year's 15th overall pick to miss Tampa Bay's last two games and severely hampered his practice schedule. Due to the nature of those injuries, Bain may never be 100 percent during his rookie campaign, which should shift expectations.

Meanwhile, Price opened the season as Seattle's lead back and showed explosive traits, with 104 combined rushing yards during the Seahawks' Week 1 and 2 victories. Unfortunately, he's now dealing with a chest injury that forced the running back onto injured reserve.

As of now, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Daylen Everette may be the most interesting name among this tier, because his playing time drastically increased after Jamel Dean suffered an ankle injury. Plus, the organization traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys last week, which means he's not coming back to provided Pittsburgh's lineup with a boost.

Patience is necessary with three highly regarded names appearing at this juncture.

The Las Vegas Raiders planned for this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, to sit and learn as the 2026 began. However, the organization could only hope to experience as good of a start as the team provided. At 3-1, with veteran Kirk Cousins playing a high level, the possibility of Mendoza entering the lineup gets pushed further and further down the road. In a best-case scenario, the reigning Heisman Trophy winner won't start a single game this season. However, the B/R Scouting Department expects he'll see the field eventually, with the Raiders facing a daunting schedule until the team's Week 13 bye. In fact, their next eight opponents own a combined 20-12 record, with only one squad currently under .500.

The Minnesota Vikings have slowly worked this year's 18th overall pick into the defensive line rotation after dealing with offseason foot surgery. Caleb Banks has played more than 16 snaps in only one contest so far. Eventually, the Vikings coaching staff will increase the interior defender's usage, then the flashes he's already showed during limited opportunities can become more consistent.

Kayden McDonald finds himself on a similar pathway as those already mentioned. McDonald has yet to play this season due to an ankle injury. However, he was designated to return from injured reserve this week, which will allow him to contribute as part of the Houston Texans' defensive rotation. McDonald could provide a significant boost to an underperforming Texans defense, specifically by making the unit even more difficult to handle at the point of attack.

A quartet of skill position performers have earned their way into specific roles for their respective squads.

The wide receiver trio of the Washington Commanders' Antonio Williams, Jacksonville Jaguars' Josh Cameron and New York Giants' Malachi Fields have each showed some play-making ability. They already combined for 25 catches, 224 yards and four touchdowns. Of the three, Williams has an opportunity to take off in the coming weeks since Terry McLaurin is nursing a hamstring injury. Though Fields' size certainly provides a different dynamic in the Giants' offense.

While Emmett Johnson finds himself behind the league's leading rusher on the Kansas City Chiefs' depth chart, the rookie has already established himself as a viable RB2 as both a runner and pass-catcher. Obviously, Kenneth Walker III will continue to carry most of the load. But Johnson is now a valuable piece in the Chiefs' third-ranked rushing offense.

Kansas City's offense has also been bolstered by undrafted free agent Kahlil Benson filling in for left tackle Josh Simmons. Benson has been protected by the scheme as a pass protector, but he does as a nice job at the point of attack to help open lanes for Walker and Johnson.

Injuries often play a big part in a prospect's evaluation. Case in point, Harold Perkins Jr. once looked like a future top-10 draft pick while playing for the LSU Tigers. His collegiate career was sidetracked by an ACL tear during the 2024 campaign. He didn't look quite the same last season. Ultimately, the linebacker fell to sixth round before being selected by the Atlanta Falcons. Over the last two weeks, Perkins' usage has nearly doubled and he's thrived. The former first-team All-SEC performer could be found making plays all over the field, especially this past weekend when he accumulated 10 tackles. Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell suffered a torn ACL in November. He was on track to be a first-round target, but the injury caused him to fall into the third frame. For a Dolphins team that lacks weapons, Bell is already its most talented target despite needing time to find his footing. The Carolina Panthers' still took offensive tackle Monroe Freeling in the first round despite limited starting experience, a high-ankle sprain during the 2025 campaign and a shoulder surgery during the previous offseason. This year's 19th overall pick still opened the season as the Panthers' starting right tackle, because Taylor Moton hasn't been cleared to play.

A heavy emphasis on offensive line play dominates this group of rookies. The Miami Dolphins' Kadyn Proctor, Detroit Lions' Blake Miller, Jacksonville Jaguars' Emmanuel Pregnon, Pittsburgh Steelers Max Iheanachor and Cleveland Browns' Austin Barber have combined to start 17 games. Proctor and Miller being instant starters wasn't a surprise after hearing their names called among this year's top 17 selections. The same can't be said of the others. Iheanachor was viewed as a developmental project. He officially became the Steelers' starting right tackle in Week 3, and Pittsburgh's run game immediately took off. Iheanachor presents the most upside of anyone among this tier and it's already started to show. Pregnon and Barber were third-round selections (two slots apart from one another). They weren't guaranteed anything upon walking into training camp. Both earned spots through competitions at guard and emerged as Day 1 starters. Tennessee Titans linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. also had to compete for playing time. He went on to capture NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month for September by leading the league with 34 total tackles through three weeks of play.

Interestingly, Caleb Downs and Jeremiyah Love were the two highest-rated players on B/R's draft board, yet neither cracked the current top-10 rookies. Downs remains super-involved in the Dallas Cowboys defense and he plays wherever he's needed within the scheme. In fact, he leads the team in total tackles. But his impact plays have been minimal. Downs is a critical component in Dallas' plans. More will be expected of him as the season progresses. As for Love, the running back hasn't been fully featured. His 55 carries are tied for 20th overall. His 223 yards lead all rookies, but the figure is still 19th overall. This year's third overall pick has yet to break off a carry of 20 yards and he's ran for only one score. To be fair, the Cardinals' propensity to fall behind opponents doesn't help matters. Conversely, the Cleveland Browns continue to draft at the highest level. After selecting Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, Quinshon Judkins and Harold Fannin Jr. last year, general manager Andrew Berry added another wave of superb talent, as evidenced by three Browns counted among the top-15 rookies. Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are already dangerous targets in the passing game. The rookies have basically surpassed veteran Jerry Jeudy to become Cleveland's top two wide receivers. Spencer Fano, who was the first offensive lineman off the board, has experienced some inconsistency, though the transition from right to left tackle looks like it'll stick long term. Now that the Browns are getting better play at quarterback, all of this young talent is being spotlighted.

Defensive rookies are far ahead of their offensive counterparts to start the 2026 campaign. The makeup of this Top 10 likely says more about the composition of the latest draft class than some all-encompassing argument over defenses being ahead of offenses early in the season because of training camp, practice and preseason limitations. Instead, the group is a reflection of this specific wave of incoming talent.

A lack of elite prospects at premium positions was the biggest knock against the 2026 class. The criticism was somewhat misplaced, though. Premium talent was available, just at different spots, which has become evident through the first four weeks of play.

Linebackers Sonny Styles and Arvell Reese, who were collegiate teammates and top-seven draft selections, have created instant impacts for the Washington Commanders and New York Giants, respectively. Styles has been particularly good using his length and athleticism in coverage, while creating multiple pressures when asked to blitz. Plus, his run fits are improving each week. Meanwhile, Reese's versatility has translated to the pro game, with 22 tackles, two tackles for loss, four pass breakups and an interception during the Giants' last two games.

Sticking with second-line defenders, Jacob Rodriguez's nose for the football didn't get lost in translation. Rodriguez currently ranks second overall with 46 total tackles. He's yet to force a fumble—which was his calling card at the collegiate level—but it's only a matter of time. Once Mansoor Delane's pure coverage ability, Hezekiah Masses' penchant for turnovers, Vega Ioane's versatility plus power at the point of attack and edge-pressure from Gabe Jacas, R Mason Thomas and Cashius Howell are factored into the question, a "down" class turns out to be highly impressive.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Hints at More Potential Trade Talks After Joey Porter Jr. Deal with Steelers
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys may not be done dealing after swinging a trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys may not be done dealing after swinging a trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

Team owner Jerry Jones said Wednesday on 105.3 The Fan that "the door is always open to get better." He added he's "never" of a mind to ignore ways for the Cowboys to improve:

Like wide receiver George Pickens in 2025, Porter joins Dallas in the final year of his rookie contract. Dallas applied the franchise tag to Pickens, so the team will have to sort out the futures of he and Porter at some point.

Jones didn't provide a clear answer when asked whether an extension for either player could be completed this season. Reading between the lines, it looks unlikely (via The Athletic's Jon Machota):

The Cowboys are 2-2 and have allowed the third-most yards in the league. So far, it's looking like a repeat of 2025, when an elite offense was canceled out by a porous defense.

From that standpoint, Dallas could benefit from another big trade. The team is running out of draft assets, though.

The Cowboys have three picks in the first six rounds of the 2027 draft, and they gave up their 2028 second-rounder to get Porter.

Especially when accounting for the cost of extensions for Porter and Pickens, the front office needs to balance out the expensive veterans with younger cost-controlled talent. That can't happen when Dallas keeps trading away picks.

Perhaps a trade emerges that's too good to pass up. Absent that, Jones would be wise to keep one eye on the outlook beyond 2026.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. signs with Vikings' practice squad after release by Giants
articles.summary: Beckham did not record a catch in three games during his return to the Giants.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. has signed with the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, the team announced Wednesday .

The 33-year-old was released by the New York Giants on Sept. 29. He played in three games after returning to the team that drafted him in 2014 and didn't record a reception. In those three games, Beckham was on the field for a total of 20 offensive snaps, with just six of those coming in his final game with the team, a 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 3.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell was Beckham's offensive coordinator when the two were with the Los Angeles Rams in 2021 when the team won Super Bowl LVI.

In eight regular-season games with the Rams, Beckham had 27 receptions for 305 yards and five touchdowns. He added 21 catches for 288 yards and two touchdowns in the postseason before he tore his ACL in the Super Bowl against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The 4-0 Vikings take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 and there is still uncertainty about the status of Justin Jefferson. The All-Pro wide receiver missed Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins with an ankle sprain . O'Connell said Tuesday that Jefferson was "doing great," but they are not sure yet how the wideout will feel on Sunday.

articles.title: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk wins his appeal on fine over his ‘Juice’ celebration
articles.summary: The 49ers fullback won his appeal over the fines issued by the NFL for what it deemed an “offensive” celebration when he imitated drinking a beverage, which the league said looked like he was chugging a beer.
articles.body: San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk won his appeal over the fines issued by the NFL for what it deemed an “offensive” celebration when he imitated drinking a beverage, which the league said looked like he was chugging a beer. Juszczyk was initially fined $29,852 for two infractions of the league’s sportsmanship rules after celebrating two catches in the third quarter of a Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins by doing the celebration he has done for years while the fans at Levi’s Stadium cheered “Juice!” for his nickname. He appealed the fine and an appeals officer ruled in his favor, the league said Wednesday. ESPN first reported that the fine had been rescinded on appeal. The NFL has vowed to crack down on celebrations this season and initially ruled that the “imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste.” Juszczyk has been doing a version of that celebration throughout his career in San Francisco in response to 49ers fans chanting his nickname after catches or other big plays. He argued in the appeal that he was imitating drinking juice. “I don’t know how else to say it. I wasn’t drinking beer in my celebration,” Juszczyk said on September 24. “I think you guys all know my nickname is Juice. I have Juice on my pads. The stadium yells ‘Juice!’ when I catch the ball. When I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice, and it’s been that way for years. So I was surprised as anybody when I got a fine this week.” Juszczyk has been the 49ers’ nominee for the Art Rooney Award for sportsmanship for the past six seasons. The only fines he previously has had were for illegal use of the helmet and low blocks. Juszczyk is in his 14th season in the NFL and 10th with San Francisco. He has made the Pro Bowl 10 times and was an All-Pro in 2023 and ’25.

articles.title: Why did the 4-0 Vikings sign Odell Beckham Jr. after his Giants return ended with 0 catches
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are undefeated through four games. Their offense has still given them a reason to call Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.body: The Minnesota Vikings are undefeated through four games. Their offense has still given them a reason to call Odell Beckham Jr.Minnesota announced Wednesday that it signed Beckham to its practice squad, one week after the New York Giants released him. ESPN reported the move after NFL insider Jordan Schultz first broke the news. Beckham did not record a catch in three games during his Giants reunion.Why did the Vikings move so quickly to sign Odell Beckham Jr.?The standings make Minnesota's move look unusual at first. The Vikings are 4-0 entering Week 5, but ESPN reported that their offense has ranked among the NFL's worst.Justin Jefferson's health is part of the equation.Jefferson suffered a sprained left ankle in Week 3, missed Week 4 and remained questionable at best for Minnesota's Week 5 matchup with the New Orleans Saints, according to ESPN.The Vikings had already added Jauan Jennings as their No. 3 receiver behind Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Jennings, however, missed one game for personal reasons and recorded two catches for nine yards on four targets in his other three appearances.That left Minnesota looking for another option.Schultz reported that the Vikings did not wait long after the Giants released Beckham on Sept. 29."The #Vikings reached out to Odell Beckham Jr. immediately after the #Giants moved on and showed significant interest. Despite a 4-0 start, the offense has needed some juice. And OBJ will try to help bring that. His relationship with Justin Jefferson is a plus, as well."Starting Beckham on the practice squad also gives Minnesota flexibility. The Vikings can evaluate how much the 33-year-old has left without immediately handing him a major offensive role.His relationship with the coaching staff helps.Beckham and Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell were together with the Los Angeles Rams when they won Super Bowl LVI. Beckham also played under Minnesota assistant head coach Frank Smith with the Miami Dolphins in 2024.Minnesota knows the player. Beckham knows people inside the building. That makes the transition less complicated than bringing in a receiver with no connection to the staff.Can Odell Beckham Jr. still help an undefeated Vikings offense that ranks among the NFL's worst?Minnesota is betting on experience, but Beckham's recent production makes this an experiment rather than a guaranteed fix.He played only 19 offensive snaps across three games for the Giants this season and did not make a catch. New York targeted him once before releasing him.Beckham also sat out the entire 2025 season. His last NFL production came with Miami in 2024, when he caught nine passes for 54 yards.There is a more encouraging recent season for Minnesota to examine.Beckham caught 35 passes for 565 yards and three touchdowns with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023. He has 575 receptions for 7,987 yards and 59 touchdowns across his NFL career, according to ESPN.His peak came much earlier. Beckham made three consecutive Pro Bowls to begin his career with the Giants and produced 1,450 receiving yards with 13 touchdowns in 2015. He followed that with 1,367 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2016.Minnesota does not need that version of Beckham to justify this move.The immediate question is whether he can give O'Connell another reliable target while Jefferson works back from his ankle injury. T.J. Hockenson entered Week 5 as Minnesota's leading receiver with 22 catches for 195 yards and a touchdown. Jefferson had 13 receptions for 179 yards and two scores, while Addison had 163 receiving yards.That production helps explain why an undefeated team went shopping.Beckham's first stop is the practice squad, so a Week 5 role is not guaranteed. Minnesota can now see how quickly he picks up the offense and how his body responds before deciding whether to elevate him.For a 4-0 team, the signing carries little immediate risk. articles.title: Christen Goff drops 'game day archives' to remind everyone that the Lions quarterback is going to be just fine
articles.summary: Christen Goff skipped Victory Monday after the Detroit Lions' loss to the Carolina Panthers but delivered a Tuesday Instagram post with a clear message.
articles.body: Trust me, Christen Goff would have much rather done a victory Monday post following the Detroit Lions game on Sunday Night Football. Unfortunately for her, the defense let her, her husband Jared and the rest of the team down. Simply put, they couldn’t stop Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers offense. So she regrouped like the veteran that she is and instead waited until Tuesday to share her "Game day archives." Victory Mondays are easy. Coming in hot on a Tuesday with a reminder that the season is long, it's by no means over, and that whatever happens the Lions quarterback is going to be just fine requires focus and discipline. articles.title: Eagles' Cam Jurgens Traded to Ravens After Lane Johnson's Retirement, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: Two of the Philadelphia Eagles' five starting offensive linemen this season are no longer on the team with Cam Jurgens getting traded one day after Lane Johnson retired.
articles.body:
Two of the Philadelphia Eagles' five starting offensive linemen this season are no longer on the team with Cam Jurgens getting traded one day after Lane Johnson retired.

The Eagles announced on Wednesday they are trading Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round draft pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection.

Johnson, who missed Philadelphia's loss to the Los Angeles Rams for personal reasons , announced on Tuesday he was retiring after 14 seasons.

"Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game. And right now my heart is telling me that it's time to say goodbye to football," Johnson wrote as part of his statement.

The decision to trade Jurgens immediately on the heels of Johnson's decision is surprising, though his performance so far this season has left something to be desired.

Per Pro Football Focus metrics (h/t Brenden Deeg of The Score), Jurgens ranks in the bottom five among 87 qualified interior offensive linemen in pass-blocking grade, pressures allowed and pass-blocking efficiency.

Jurgens is under contract through the 2029 season after signing a four-year, $68 million extension in April 2025. His cap hits in the next three seasons, not including 2026, are $9.2 million, $12.3 million and $16.3 million.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jurgens is currently in concussion protocol and not likely to play in Week 5. He is expected to make his Ravens debut against the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 18.

The Ravens entered this season with Jovaughn Gwyn as their starting center after losing Tyler Linderbaum to the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency.

Gwyn suffered a fractured fibula in Baltimore's Week 3 win over the Dallas Cowboys that will keep him out for at least two to three months. Olaivavega Ioane, the No. 14 pick in the 2026 NFL draft, moved from guard to center in Week 4 and didn't allow a pressure in 34 pass-blocking snaps against the Tennessee Titans.

The addition of Jurgens allows the Ravens to shift Ioane back to right guard. If Jurgens returns to the form in Baltimore that made him a two-time Pro Bowler with the Eagles, the trade cost will be a small price to pay.

Philadelphia turned a player it seemed to lose faith in into a potentially valuable second-round pick in the 2028 draft that can be used to select a young player or potentially package in another trade to add a piece that can help the roster right now.

articles.summary: The Eagles are further shaking up their offensive line by trading two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens.
articles.body:
Two aspiring NFL playoff contenders swung a trade on Wednesday, Oct. 7, to reshape their shaky offensive fronts.

The Philadelphia Eagles agreed to send two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round draft pick to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, the Ravens announced.

Jurgens helps fill a void on the interior for the Ravens, who lost three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum to the Las Vegas Raiders this offseason. With initial replacements Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocci sidelined with long-term injuries, the Ravens shifted first-round pick Vega Ioane, who was drafted as a guard, to center in a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans .

"We are excited to acquire a two-time Pro Bowl center, Cam Jurgens, from the Eagles in a trade," Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta said in a statement. "Cam is a player we have long admired going all the way back to the draft process. He's a young foundational piece along our offensive line – a great scheme and cultural fit who will contribute quickly in Baltimore. We are confident that Cam will significantly impact our team and community."

Jurgens succeeded Jason Kelce in Philadelphia but also shifted to guard this season in light of offensive guard Landon Dickerson landing on injured reserve after Week 1. The deal comes one day after linchpin right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement .

Jurgens landed in the NFL's concussion protocol after a 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.

A second-round pick out of Nebraska in 2022, Jurgens, 27, is in the second year of a four-year, $68 million contract extension.

articles.title: ESPN Expert Gives Honest Assessment of Chiefs After 4-0 Start
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are off to a perfect 4-0 start, but their unbeaten record does not necessarily mean they have looked like a dominant team. An ESPN exp...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are off to a perfect 4-0 start, but their unbeaten record does not necessarily mean they have looked like a dominant team. An ESPN expert offered an honest assessment of the Chiefs after their narrow 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, pointing to reasons for optimism as well as concerns that could become more significant later in the season.

Kansas City has found ways to win each of its first four games , which remains the most important takeaway from its early schedule. However, the Chiefs have not consistently overwhelmed opponents, and their latest victory showed how little margin for error they currently have. They needed a late touchdown to secure the win after the Raiders pushed them throughout the contest.

The close games have raised questions about whether Kansas City is playing at the level expected from a team that has become a perennial Super Bowl contender. The Chiefs have the experience and talent to overcome difficult situations, but relying on late-game heroics every week is not a sustainable formula once the schedule becomes more difficult.

There are still plenty of reasons for confidence. The offense has continued to produce explosive moments, while the defense has done enough to keep games within reach. Kansas City has also shown an ability to respond when opponents make runs, an important trait for a team that expects to remain in contention throughout the season.

ESPN Expert Assesses Kansas City Chiefs After Impressive 4-0 Start

Kansas City was given a positive review after starting the season with a 4-0 record . This can be seen in an analysis by Dan Graziano for ESPN.

There are no perfect teams. There are other very good ones, even in the AFC. The Jaguars might be the best team in the league when all is said and done. So could the Bills. The 49ers might be, too! The Browns … nah, let's not go there. But none of the other very good teams in the league has the history of high-level winning that Andy Reid and Mahomes have together. So, if you want to tell me that Kansas City is the best, I'd have a hard time mounting an argument that I truly believe in.

The emergence of Kenneth Walker III has provided another encouraging development for the Chiefs. His late touchdown production against Las Vegas helped Kansas City escape with the victory and demonstrated how a stronger rushing presence could take pressure off the passing game. If the running attack continues to improve, the Chiefs could become more balanced as the season progresses.

The 4-0 record gives Kansas City an excellent foundation, but its early performances suggest there is still work to do before it can be considered a complete team. The Chiefs have shown they can win close games, and the next step will be proving they can consistently control them against stronger competition.

articles.title: Jerry Jones claims no one has a better future than Tony Romo: ‘He’s just getting started’
articles.summary: Tony Romo’s future as a lead NFL analyst with CBS might be finished, but Jerry Jones believes the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback still has a great future...
articles.body:
Tony Romo's future as a lead NFL analyst with CBS might be finished, but Jerry Jones believes the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback still has a great future ahead of him.

After placing Romo on indefinite leave shortly after his OWI arrest in Wisconsin over the summer, CBS finally decided to part ways with its now-former lead NFL analyst last week . Without Romo, CBS has placed J.J. Watt in their lead analyst chair alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson. Without CBS, Romo can now seek other employment opportunities while still recouping most of the $72 million remaining on his contract. And with that freedom, Jerry Jones believes Romo's future is bright.

Jones joined 105.3 The Fan's Shan Shariff and RJ Choppy Wednesday morning in one of his regular weekly spots on the station. And upon being asked about Romo, Jones spoke glowingly of the former Cowboys quarterback.

"Tony is one of the most valued relationships that I have on a personal basis," Jones admitted. "I love him, and I'm sorry that this has evolved this way this year because I enjoyed him so much in what he could bring to the NFL and, frankly, I was proud of him as a former Cowboy. Now, having said all of that, he's just getting started. He really is. I say that with all sincerity. He's just getting started.

"And he certainly has made some mistakes. I can't look in my mirror without seeing what can happen when you experience mistakes. But he realizes that there's an area of his life that he wants to do better in. That's been said ad nauseam, publicly. He's got great opportunity ahead of him. I don't know of anyone, period, that has a better future than Tony Romo. And I'm excited for him. He's not only got great talent, but he's a hell of a man."

This obviously isn't the way Romo wanted his tenure with CBS to end. And while it's not the way CBS expected it to end either, some have argued the network sought the opportunity to move on from Romo before his contract was up, and the OWI was just their excuse to do it.

Without CBS, the future can still be bright for Romo. As Awful Announcing's Sean Keeley explained last week , Romo deserves to be criticized and punished for impaired driving. But it doesn't have to be career-ending. And in a forgiving society, it won't be the end of Romo's career.

It might not be in a lead chair on CBS, NBC, or Fox, but Jerry Jones is right to believe Romo will have opportunities to talk about the NFL again. Romo said he will take some time off in the wake of his OWI arrest and parting with CBS. Maybe that's just this season, maybe it's longer. But when Romo is ready to get back on TV, big offers will come his way.

On Valentine's Day in 2027 (Feb. 14), Super Bowl 61 will be broadcast on ESPN , marking the network's first time showing the game, but it will also be available on the Disney+ streaming service .

ESPN announced that the game would be broadcast on Disney+ on Feb. 14, 2027. This is a third option for fans to watch it besides ESPN and ABC.

Troy Aikman and Joe Buck will call the game , with Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge also present. A ManningCast alternative broadcast will also air with Peyton and Eli Manning. This marks their first time doing a broadcast during the Super Bowl. However, unlike their regular broadcasts, they will be live in Los Angeles during the Super Bowl.

How to watch ESPN's Super Bowl 61 in February 2027 on Disney+

The Super Bowl can be watched on traditional TV channels like ABC and ESPN. Disney+ subscribers will also be able to stream it on the platform.

Fans not at SoFi Stadium will have several options to enjoy the game. It marks the first time ESPN has broadcast the game (ABC last aired a Super Bowl in 2006).

The game will be played at SoFi Stadium, the home of the Los Angeles Chargers and Rams, on Feb. 14. SoFi Stadium also hosted the game in 2022 when the Rams beat the Cincinnati Bengals.

Who will play in the game is still being decided. The Seattle Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots in the game last year, which was played at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California.
