articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins' status up in the air ahead of Week 5 road game vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: Both Chase and Higgins have recorded more than 200 receiving yards this season.
articles.body:
Having dropped back-to-back contests, the Cincinnati Bengals entered Week 5 with a potential get-right game on the horizon. The 2-2 Bengals can return to the win column on Sunday in Miami against the rebuilding, 0-4 Dolphins.

But Cincinnati may have to get creative offensively in order to get back on track, considering that its top two wideouts are navigating injuries.

Ja'Marr Chase is still going through the league's protocol after suffering a concussion in a 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last weekend, head coach Zac Taylor told reporters on Wednesday. Tee Higgins, who's dealing with an adductor injury he sustained down the stretch of that defeat, will be limited in practice .

Chase and Higgins — two of the 15 highest-paid wide receivers in the NFL, in terms of average annual value, according to Over the Cap — have recorded more than 200 receiving yards this season.

Higgins, a 2020 second-round draft pick out of Clemson, leads the team with 25 catches and 401 receiving yards. Chase, the 2021 No. 5 overall pick, is tied for second with 21 grabs, and his 212 receiving yards are good for the second most of any Bengal this season. The three touchdown receptions Chase has made are tied for first on the team.

They are quarterback Joe Burrow's go-to targets in an offense that just attempted 54 passes and ran the ball only 15 times versus the Jags.

At the moment, Cincinnati ranks second to last in the NFL with 74.3 rushing yards per game. It's tied for 26th with 3.6 yards per carry.

While Burrow told reporters postgame this past Sunday that he's open to throwing even more , doing so will not only further compromise the team's offensive balance, but it will also be more difficult given the Bengals' depleted receiving corps.

Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve with a thumb issue that required surgery. Rookie Colbie Young went down with a knee injury in a Week 3 setback to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In the absence of Chase and Higgins over the weekend, attention turned to wide receivers Mitch Tinsley and Dohnte Meyers, as well as tight end Mike Gesicki.

Tinsley, who reeled in a pair of touchdown passes for Cincinnati last season but most recently was on the Houston Texans' practice squad, snagged three balls for 49 yards against the Jaguars. Meyers, a former CFL standout , finished with seven receptions and 82 yards. Gesicki went for three catches, 40 yards and one score.

Fortunately for Burrow, the Dolphins are allowing passers to complete 77.9% of their attempts. Only the Dallas Cowboys (8.0) and Arizona Cardinals (8.0) are giving up more net yards per pass attempt than Miami (7.7) this season .

articles.title: Rams Bracing for Crucial Decision on Myles Garrett as Return Timeline Remains Fluid
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay provided an update on Myles Garrett as the star pass rusher works through his recovery from knee surgery. Garrett land...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay provided an update on Myles Garrett as the star pass rusher works through his recovery from knee surgery. Garrett landed on injured reserve after his team debut, keeping him unavailable while he recovers.

Initial projections pointed to an extended absence, but McVay noted steady progress in the pass rusher's rehabilitation. The Rams plan to evaluate his status later this week to determine the next steps in his return.

Sean McVay discusses Myles Garrett recovery ahead of medical review

Garrett has not played since Week 1 and will stay on injured reserve for at least one more game as he continues rehabbing his surgically repaired knee. The injury designation requires him to miss a minimum of four games, a threshold that was met heading into Week 5.

Speaking to reporters during his Monday press conference, McVay acknowledged the ongoing recovery process without confirming an exact target date. 'I know he's making really good progress,' McVay said . 'We haven't talked specifics like that.'

The head coach noted he will consult with Reggie Scott, the team's senior vice president of sports medicine, to establish a definitive timeline ahead of Thursday's briefing. Reports in late September suggested a six-week recovery window that would push a possible debut past this week's Cardinals game, though McVay said he was not familiar with that specific timeline.

Garrett set the NFL single-season sack record with 23 sacks last year and won his second Defensive Player of the Year award in the process. He played just 62% of Los Angeles' defensive snaps in the opener and did not record a tackle or a sack before exiting. Garrett later admitted knee swelling had limited him for most of training camp.

Rams await Myles Garrett's return after blockbuster trade

The Rams acquired Garrett to fortify their pass rush, cementing one of the biggest moves of the NFL offseason.

Los Angeles finally completed the blockbuster trade on June 1, sending Jared Verse and first-, second- and third-round picks in 2027, 2028 and 2029 to Cleveland for Garrett. The Rams also reworked his contract into a $204 million deal days after the trade closed.

Garrett has played in just one game for Los Angeles since his arrival. Los Angeles hosts Arizona in Week 6 and visits Washington in Week 9, two potential return windows.

articles.body:
Washington Commanders fans experienced horrible déjà vu in Week 2 upon seeing quarterback Jayden Daniels go down with another dislocated elbow . But their fears may have been overblown, as the quarterback appears on schedule to return to action in Week 5.

Daniels was spotted throwing Wednesday and is expected to be listed as a full participant in practice ahead of a possible return against the New York Giants on Sunday.

Daniels' practice status shouldn't necessarily come as a surprise. Despite dealing with the injury last week, Daniels was able to put in limited practice every single day. Ultimately, he was ruled out for the team's Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts in London, but it was a sign Daniels was closer to returning than expected.

Disaster struck during that contest, however, as backup quarterback Marcus Mariota left the game with a knee injury that's expected to keep him sidelined for multiple weeks. With Daniels also out for that game, the Commanders were forced to turn to third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis. While the rookie did throw his first NFL touchdown, he couldn't lead the team all the way back in a 30-13 loss.

While it looked as though Kaliakmanis was set up for multiple starts, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that wasn't the case after the loss. Quinn told reporters the hope was for Daniels to return against the Giants in Week 5. The coach doubled down on those comments the following day, saying Daniels would get all the practice reps and start in Week 5 . Quinn added that Daniels wanted to play in Week 4, but the team opted to play it cautious. The team reportedly took a similar approach with wideout Terry McLaurin, who could also return to action in Week 5, though was reportedly working off to the side during practice Wednesday.

With Daniels back, the Commanders should be in a much better spot moving forward. If the team has any hope of shaking off its 1-3 start, Daniels' return feels like a reason for optimism.

The team should still harbor some concern about Daniels moving forward. The quarterback battled the same injury last year and was forced to leave his first game back after aggravating the injury.

The Commanders will have to hope he avoids that same fate this time around, and is able to lead the team out of its early hole and get back into playoff contention.
